cos_cname: 有機光電顯示材料及元件
memo:
1.第一至第三階段限材料系、奈米所加選，開學後加退選開放外系或外校加選
[English Medium Course]
cos_ename: Organic Electro-Optical Display Materials and Devices
dep_ename: Department of Materials Science and Engineering
crs_outline:
簡介有機半導體(含介電材料)、有機光電(含光學及非線性光學材料)、AI矽光子(含光纖及光調變器材料)、及軟性電子(含高分子封裝複合材料)等材料及其元件之原理與分析
Introduction to organic semiconductors (including dielectric materials), organic optoelectronics (including optical and nonlinear optical materials), AI silicon photonics (including optical fiber and optical modulator materials), and flexible electronics (including polymer packaging composite materials) and the principles and analysis of their components.

課程綱要(Outline)：
A. 材料性質介紹 (Introduction to Properties of Materials)
1. 材料電學性質 (Electrical Properties of Materials)
2. 材料熱學性質 (Thermal Properties of Materials)
3. 材料光學性質 (Optical Properties of Materials)

B. 高分子材料簡介 (Introduction to Polymer Materials)
1. 高分子材料化學 (Polymer Materials Chemistry)
2. 高分子材料物理 (Polymer Materials Physics)
3. 高分子材料應用 (Applications of Polymer Materials)：液晶高分子材料 LC Polymer Materials、導電高分子材料Conducting Polymer Materials、發光二極體高分子材料 Light Emitting Diode (LED) Polymer Materials、非線性光學高分子材料 Nonlinear Optical (NLO) Polymer Materials、電光高分子材料 Electro-Optic (EO) Polymer Materials Materials

C. 液晶顯示材料及元件 (LC Display Materials and Devices)
1. 液晶材料基本介紹 (Introduction to LCs)
1.1.1.	液晶分類 (Classification of LCs)
1.1.2.	化學結構及物理性質(Chemical Structures and Physical Properties)
2. 液晶之應用物性與量測 (Introduction to LCs)
2.1. 液晶電學及光學性質 (Electrical and Optical Properties of LCs)
2.2. 液晶光電效應 (Electro-Optical Properties of LCs)
3. 液晶顯示相關原理及元件 (Principle and Devices of LCDs)
3.1. 液晶顯示器原理 (Principle of LCDs)
3.2. TN液晶顯示器 (TN LCDs)
3.3. STN液晶顯示器 (STN LCDs)
3.4.鐵電液晶顯示器 (Ferroelectric LCDs)
3.5. PDLC顯示器 (PDLC Displays)
3.6. TFT液晶顯示器 (TFT LCDs)
3.7. 其他改良型液晶顯示器 (MVA, WVA, IPS LCDs)
4. 液晶顯示相關元件材料及製程 (Device Materials and Process of LCDs)
4.1. 液晶顯示器製程 (Process of LCDs)
4.2. 液晶顯示相關元件材料：透明基板 (Substrate)、透明電極 (ITO)、配向層 (Alignment Layer)、間隙物 (Spacer)、彩色濾光片 (Color Filter)、偏光板 (Polarizer)、補償膜 (Compensation Film)、及光源及導光配件 (Backlighting System)

D. 有機發光二極體顯示材料及元件 (OLED and PLED Display Materials and Devices)
1. 有機發光二極體材料基本介紹 (Introduction to OLED and PLED Materials)
1.1. 化學結構 (Chemical Structures)
1.2. 物理性質 (Physical Properties)
2. 有機發光二極體之應用物性與量測 (Physical Properties and Measurements of OLEDs)
3. 有機發光二極體相關原理及元件 (Principle and Devices of OLEDs and PLEDs)
4. 有機發光二極體相關材料及製程 (Device Materials and Process of OLEDs and PLEDs)
4.1. 有機發光二極體製程 (Process of OLEDs and PLEDs)
4.2. 電極基板 (Electrode and Substrate of OLEDs and PLEDs)
4.3. 發光層 (Light-Emitting Layer)
4.4. 電子傳輸層 (Electron Transporting Layer)
4.5. 電洞傳輸層 (Hole Transporting Layer)

E. 有機及高分子太陽能電池材料及元件 (Organic and Polymer Solar Cell Materials and Devices)
1. 有機及高分子太陽能電池材料基本介紹 (Introduction to Organic and Polymer Solar Cell Materials)
2. 有機及高分子太陽能電池之應用物性與量測 (Physical Properties and Measurements of Organic and Polymer Solar Cells)
3. 有機及高分子太陽能電池相關原理及元件 (Principle and Devices of Organic and Polymer Solar Cells)

cos_ename: Advanced Semiconductor Technologies and Global Industry Strategies
dep_ename: Department of Materials Science and Engineering
crs_outline: The course aims to provide students with comprehensive knowledge and practical skills across various aspects of semiconductor technology. Students will explore characterization techniques and their applications in analyzing material properties, learn statistical tools to evaluate device reliability, and address critical challenges such as dielectric breakdown and bias instability. The course also covers radiation effects on semiconductors, 2D materials' unique properties and applications, and the design and operation of optoelectronic devices. Additionally, students will delve into advanced topics such as spintronics, ferroic materials, and their device applications. The curriculum emphasizes the semiconductor industry's evolution, including R&D management, global supply chain dynamics, and business models. Finally, the course fosters creative problem-solving skills, equipping students to address complex challenges in the high-tech industry and innovate within a rapidly evolving technological landscape.

cos_ename: Synchrotron X-ray in Materials Science Research
dep_ename: Department of Materials Science and Engineering
crs_outline:
推廣同步輻射應用研究，培訓同步輻射X光繞射，X光散射，X光吸收，X光影像研究及應用人才
This is an entrance level course to provide students with the basic knowledge about the properties of an accelerator based light sources and its applications in characterizing structural, physical, and chemical properties of materials. The theory and experimental methods of X-ray diffraction/scattering, spectroscopy and x-ray imaging and their applications in various research fields will be covered. The primarily applications are in solid state sciences of current interests, such as new electronic and magnetic materials, thin films, energy materials, and surface and interface structure.

memo: 材料科學與工程學系優先
dep_ename: Department of Materials Science and Engineering
crs_outline:
本課程希望同學在學習後能墊定扎實的化學及相關科學基礎。課程首先將從微觀，即量子力學的觀點出發去探討原子和分子模型，以及化學鍵結的基本理論。其次利用物質三態的性質，簡單闡述微觀和巨觀的觀點和與之間的連結。最後為了進一步理解巨觀觀點下能量以及物質的變化，將介紹熱力學定律的基本概念。
This course is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in chemistry and related sciences. It begins with a microscopic perspective rooted in quantum mechanics, introducing atomic and molecular models as well as the fundamental theories of chemical bonding. Next, the course uses the properties of the three states of matter to illustrate the connection between microscopic and macroscopic viewpoints. Finally, to deepen understanding of energy and material transformations about the macroscopic viewpoint, the course introduces the basic principles of thermodynamics.

crs_outline:
「太空動力學」英文為Astrodynamics，其主要研究範疇為在牛頓運動定律與重力定律下，火箭、飛彈與太空飛行器的運動行為。太空動力學主要關心各種太空飛行器從發射、入軌到重返大氣層的運動軌跡，同時也包括了軌道轉換與星際飛行。「太空動力學」是以天體力學為基礎，隨著人類發射第一顆人造衛星Sputnik-1後逐步發展，加入許多新的元素，包括火箭推進、空氣動力學、衛星工程等不同學門，成為一門綜合性的學科。

本課程除涵蓋古典二體問題，討論軌道的初始值與邊界值問題外，也包括現代衛星軌道計算與設計等單元，適合應用數學、物理、太空遙測、航太機械或是對太空動力學有興趣的大四與研究所同學選修。

memo: 核心選修課程。開4/研  [English Medium Course]
crs_outline:
微流體系統提供了一個方便的自動化平台供多種生物醫療相關的研究與微奈米機器人開發。許多商業產品相應而生主要因為微流體系統的低感染、低成本、高速等種種優點。本課程將從最基礎微流體系統開始介紹。並從知名期刊以及研討會中挑選論文，在課堂中以互動的方式討論。透過此課程學生不只能夠對微流體系統與趨勢有初步的認識，並能了解怎麼去搜尋、閱讀、並審查一般科學文獻。[本門課為英文授課]

Microfluidic system provides a convenient platform of automation for biological and medical tests as well as the development of micor-nano scale robots. Different products have been developed in the market because of its advantages of low-contamination, low-cost, high-speed and etc. In this course, we will first introduce the fundamentals of microfluidic systems. After that, we will interactively discuss the cutting-edge technologies from selected works from journals or top-rank conferences. Through this course, students will 
- Identify and describe the fundamental concepts of microfluidics.
- Apply microfluidic principles to analyze biological and medical systems.
- Critique and evaluate recent microfluidics papers.
- Design and present a novel microfluidic system for a biomedical application.

crs_outline:
本課程學習以時域/頻域之數學函數分析與理論推導方式進行訊號與系統之處理與轉換,以協助解決實際工程設計問題, 課程內容為
1. 時域/頻域訊號表示方式與系統構成之基本觀念，訊號之捲積（convolution）演算。
2. Fourier, Laplace, Z 轉換之數理函數理論發展, 包括
  -Fourier series and transform: CTFS/DTFS/CTFT/DTFT/DFT/FFT/Short time FT(音訊分析).
  -Laplace transform 及 系統建模
  -取樣定理，訊號混疊 (Aliasing) 
  -Z 轉換及離散時間系統建模
3. 數位濾波器架構, IIR/FIR 濾波器設計與程式實現
4. 瞭解工程或物理現象與數學描述模式之間的關係
5. 如何將訊號與系統理論設計逐步實現在實際工程應用: FFT 程式,數位濾波器程式,PID控制器程式
This course contains a comprehensive treatment of continuous-time and discrete-time signals,systems and transforms, from their theoretical mathematical foundations to practical implementation in engineering.
1. Signals and systems mathematical definition, the characteristics and the properties. Convolution of signals.
2. Fourier Series (FS), Fourier Transform (FT), and analysis in continuous and discrete time domain, including
  -CTFS/DTFS/CTFT/DTFT/DFT/FFT/Short Time FT.
  -Laplace Transform and System Modeling.
  -z-transform and Discrete-Time System Modeling.
3. Digital filter structures and Digital filters design: IIR/FIR
4. Applications to digital signal processing and control
5. FFT programming, Digital Filters programming, PID controller programming

This course is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in chemistry and related sciences. It begins with a microscopic perspective rooted in quantum mechanics, introducing atomic and molecular models as well as the fundamental theories of chemical bonding. Next, the course uses the properties of the three states of matter to illustrate the connection between microscopic and macroscopic viewpoints. Finally, to deepen understanding of energy and material transformations about the macroscopic viewpoint, the course introduces the basic principles of thermodynamics.

cos_cname: 自旋電子感測與智慧計算
memo: 建議修過普通物理，微積分及工程數學。
crs_outline:
自旋電子學（Spintronics）利用電子自旋進行感測、資訊儲存與運算，已廣泛應用於磁場感測器、磁性記憶體、神經型態運算及量子感測等領域。本課程將介紹自旋電子學之基本物理原理、磁性薄膜材料、磁阻效應、自旋軌道耦合與磁化動力學等核心概念，並探討其於智慧感測與新型運算架構中的應用。
除理論基礎外，本課程強調實驗實作與研究訓練。學生將接觸磁性薄膜製備、磁性量測與自旋動力學分析技術，包括實際操作超高真空磁控濺鍍系統（Ultra-High Vacuum Magnetron Sputtering）、磁光克爾效應量測（Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect, MOKE）及自旋轉矩鐵磁共振量測（Spin-Torque Ferromagnetic Resonance, ST-FMR）等實驗平台，學習自旋電子元件從材料製備、元件特性分析到感測應用之完整研究流程。
課程亦將介紹磁阻式感測器、磁性記憶體、磁振子元件及新興量子磁感測技術，使學生掌握自旋電子感測與智慧計算之最新研究發展與未來趨勢。

課程目標 :
1. 理解自旋電子學之基本物理原理與磁性材料特性。
2. 熟悉GMR、TMR、STT、SOT等重要自旋電子效應及元件操作機制。
3. 瞭解磁性感測器、MRAM及新型智慧計算元件之設計原理與應用。
4. 學習磁性薄膜之製程技術與材料特性分析方法。
5. 實際操作超高真空磁控濺鍍系統（UHV Magnetron Sputtering），了解磁性薄膜與異質結構之製備流程。
6. 實際進行磁光克爾效應（MOKE）量測，分析磁滯曲線、磁異向性與磁化反轉行為。
7. 認識並操作自旋轉矩鐵磁共振（ST-FMR）量測系統，學習磁化動力學與自旋軌道力矩分析方法。
8. 培養進入自旋電子、磁性感測、量子感測及智慧計算相關研究領域之基礎能力。
Spintronics exploits the spin degree of freedom of electrons for sensing, information storage, and computation, and has been widely applied in magnetic sensors, magnetic memory devices, neuromorphic computing, and quantum sensing technologies. This course introduces the fundamental physical principles of spintronics, including magnetic thin-film materials, magnetoresistive effects, spin–orbit coupling, and magnetization dynamics. The course further explores the applications of spintronic devices in intelligent sensing systems and emerging computing architectures.

In addition to theoretical foundations, the course emphasizes hands-on laboratory training and research-oriented learning. Students will gain experience in magnetic thin-film fabrication, magnetic characterization, and spin dynamics analysis through direct operation of advanced experimental platforms, including an Ultra-High Vacuum (UHV) Magnetron Sputtering System, Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect (MOKE) Measurement System, and Spin-Torque Ferromagnetic Resonance (ST-FMR) Measurement System. Through these activities, students will learn the complete research workflow of spintronic devices, from material synthesis and device characterization to sensing applications.

The course also covers magnetoresistive sensors, magnetic memory technologies, magnonic devices, and emerging quantum sensing techniques, enabling students to understand the latest developments and future trends in spintronic sensing and intelligent computing.

Course Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

Understand the fundamental physical principles of spintronics and the properties of magnetic materials.
Explain the operating mechanisms of key spintronic effects and devices, including GMR, TMR, STT, and SOT.
Understand the design principles and applications of magnetic sensors, MRAM, and emerging intelligent computing devices.
Learn fabrication techniques and characterization methods for magnetic thin films.
Operate an Ultra-High Vacuum (UHV) Magnetron Sputtering System and understand the fabrication processes of magnetic thin films and heterostructures.
Perform Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect (MOKE) measurements and analyze magnetic hysteresis loops, magnetic anisotropy, and magnetization reversal behavior.
Understand and perform Spin-Torque Ferromagnetic Resonance (ST-FMR) measurements for the investigation of magnetization dynamics and spin–orbit torques.
Develop the fundamental skills required for research in spintronics, magnetic sensing, quantum sensing, and intelligent computing.

The objective of this course is that students will be introduced to and become familiar with the mechanical behavior of structural members subjected to a variety of different loading situations (axial tension, compression, shear force, torsion, bending and combined loadings).

Chapter 3: Torsion
Chapter 4: Shear Force and Bending Moment
Chapter 5: Bending and Shear Stresses in Beams

This is a one-semester required course in differential equations. As a student majoring in physics, this subject is very helpful in your future coursework such as electrodynamics and quantum physics. More importantly, you will learn Fourier analysis and Laplace methods which are core knowledge in studying optics and electronic circuits. 

The following topics will be covered.
1. First-order differential equations
2. Second-order linear differential equations
3. Higher-order linear differential equations
4. Series solutions of first-order and second-order linear equations
5. Systems of first-order linear equations
6. The Laplace transform
7. Partial differential equations and Fourier series
8. Boundary value problems

crs_outline:
Electromagnetism is the knowledge about how electric and magnetic forces work.
The course starts from the classic experiments that discovered/investigated the electromagnetic interactions, and then we apply vector algebra (gradient, divergence, and curl) to reformulate the phenomenology. The upgraded math provides a general form, allowing us to derive the electromagnetic energy and forces in 2D and 3D.
The course is designed for the second- and third-year undergraduate students.
The course covers the necessary math (coordinate system and vector analysis), electrostatics, electric force in matter, magnetostatics, and magnetic force in matter.
With the support from this course, students will be able to (Intended Learning Outcomes):
(1) Identify electromagnetic force and energy, and explain how it works
(2) Derive electromagnetic force and potential fields using vector algebra
(3) Define how electric and magnetic force influence the electric charges and magnetic dipoles in matter, and then formulate the electromagnetic fields in matter (dielectrics, conductors, diamagnets, paramagnets, ferromagnets)
(4) Integrate the theories of electric and magnetic fields, leading to Maxwell’s equations and the discovery of electromagnetic waves.

電磁學描述電力和磁力如何運作。
本課程介紹發現/研究電磁交互作用的經典實驗，然後我們使用向量微積分（梯度、散度和旋度）來重新表達電磁學的理論。升級版的數學工具幫助我們在二維和三維空間推導出電力/磁力和能量的分佈。
本課程是為大學二年級和三年級學生設計的。
本課程會教必要的數學（坐標系統和向量分析）、靜電學、物質中電力如何運作、靜磁學和物質中磁力如何運作。
修習本課程，學生將學會（預期學習成果）：
(1) 辨識電磁力和能量，並解釋其運作原理
(2) 利用向量代數推導電力/磁力和位能場
(3) 定義電力和磁力如何影響物質中的電荷和磁偶極子，推導物質中的電磁場（電介質、導體、抗磁體、順磁體、鐵磁體）
(4)整合電場和磁場理論，最終促成Maxwell方程組和電磁波的發現。

memo: [English Medium Course]
crs_outline:
"Statistical Physics II"  course ventures into the rich possible behavior of complex and many-body systems responding to external influences, undergoing collective ordering via phase transitions, exhibiting universal scaling phenomena, and evolving under non-equilibrium conditions. A cornerstone of this advanced understanding is Mean Field Theory, which, despite its approximations,  provides an invaluable first step and conceptual framework for understanding phase transitions and spontaneous symmetry breaking. To move beyond mean-field approximations and to systematically incorporate fluctuations, particularly near critical points, the course introduces Statistical Field Theory. 
This powerful approach reformulates statistical mechanics problems in the language of quantum field theory,  enabling the use of tools like Functional Integrals. Functional integration provides a versatile and elegant method for averaging over microscopic degrees of freedom, calculating partition functions, and deriving effective theories for collective modes. 
Field-theoretic methodologies are indispensable for a comprehensive grasp of Linear Response Theory, which relates microscopic fluctuations to macroscopic observables, and for the precise application of the Renormalization Group (RG).  The RG, consequently, offers profound insights into universality, scaling, and the characteristics of continuous phase 
transitions. Furthermore, the course introduces Non-equilibrium Statistical Physics, extending these equilibrium frameworks to systems subjected to external forces or those not yet thermalized. Expertise in these integrated topics is critical for researchers in fields such as condensed matter physics and materials science, providing the essential theoretical apparatus for analyzing diverse phenomena, interpreting experiments, developing models, and contributing to contemporary physics.

memo: [English Medium Course]
crs_outline:
In this course, we will go though the basic knowledge and skills to work with biological soft matter.

The 1st part introduces the bio material, including thermotropic liquid crystal, lyotropic liquid crystal, colloids, and biological polymer. We will introduce phase transitions, and demonstrate how to identify the phases and microstucture under microscopes. The electrical, mechanical, and optical properties of the bio soft matter will be discussed, especially, how the structure of the molecule determines the physical properties.

The 2nd part is propagation of light in birefringent material. The birefringence leads to ordinary and extraordinary modes of light propagation, and switches the polarization state of light. The theory will be derived. Additionally, bio materials are chiral materials. They show optical activity. We will investigate how the chirality +  birefringence lead to reflection, transmission, and scattering of light.
This part consist of two art & craft experiments:
(1) Collage of tapes: students will learn how birefringence colors show the orientation of molecules, which is the essential idea of polarized optical microscopy.
(2) Cellulose photonic crystals: it shows the three stable states of chiral liquid crystal, which is the essential idea of colored electronic paper. 

The 3nd part is about the four typical liquid crystal operation modes, which are In-Plane-Switching (IPS), Vertically Aligned (VA), Electrically Controlled Birefringence (ECB), and Twisted Nematic (TN). We will analyze the cell structure, the materials, the assembly, the operation, and their characteristic properties.

Finally we explore the novel bio optoelectronics, such as electronic ink, chromogenic medical reagents, bio electronics and quantum photonics ...etc.


在本課程中，我們會介紹生物物質基本的物理性質，還有如何操作生物光電材料。
第一部分介紹生物材料：熱致型液晶、溶致型液晶、膠體、和生物高分子。我們會介紹物質的相與相變，以及如何用顯微鏡辨識液晶相。我們會討論生物物質的電子、機械、光學性質，以及分子結構如何決定物理性質。

第二部份探討光如何在雙折射物質中傳播。光在雙折射物質中會分解成尋常光與非尋常光，兩種傳播模式的相位差可以用來切換光的偏極態。生物物質還有手性(旋光性)，我們會繼續討論手性結構如何造成旋光穿透/反射/散射。
此部份做兩個美勞實驗：
(1)膠帶拼貼畫：體驗如何用雙折射色判斷分子指向(偏光顯微術的基本原理)。
(2)纖維素光子晶體：體驗手性液晶三穩態(彩色電子紙的基本原理)。

第三部分介紹四種典型的液晶(向列型物質)的操作模式，分別是水平操作模式(IPS)、垂直操作模式(VA)、電控雙折射模式(ECB)和扭轉操作模式(TN)。我們將分析元件的結構、材料、如何組裝、如何操作及其特性。

最後我們探討新穎生物光電元件，例如：電子墨水、顯色式醫學試片、生物電子 / 光量子元件...等等。

crs_outline: 此課程強調人因工程之心理要素，用以剖析人類之於環境、產品、介面、組織、系統的決策行為。該學門可進一步細分為認知以及組織人因工程 (Cognitive and Organizational Ergonomics)，學生將學習到如何以工程角度探討人類認知。該課程將介紹認知人因工程（Cognitive ergonomics）之基礎以及相關應用原理，學生可透過所學知識探究認知人因工程於相關產業之應用；課程後半段將介紹組織人因工程(Organizational / Macro-ergonomics)，幫助學生學習認知人因工程於組織、系統上的運用，期望為往後工業管理之相關決策提供啟發。

4.介紹企業流動資產(Current Assets)會計科目的揭露作業流程及其應用。
5.詳細闡述會計科目、習題講解與會計原理原則，輔助學生紮實學習。

4. Introduce the concept and application of current assets.
5. Provide detailed explanations of accounting subjects, exercises and accounting principles, to assist students in solid learning.

crs_outline: The objective of this course is to provide the students with the fundamental concepts of logistics management and its related operations and decisions. The course starts with the background, role, and importance of logistics management. Then, the components in the logistics management are introduced together with its functions and targets. The major components include demand forecasting, inventory and supply management, logistics system design (including facility location analysis) and transportation planning and control. Besides, the concept of supply chain integration will be emphasized, and the contemporary issues will be addressed. Several real-world short cases will be discussed to further illustrate the key concepts and the potential practical application. In addition to the topics listed above, the course will also emphasize the application of the spreadsheet software and optimization tool to build up students' basic skills to solve logistics decision problems.

crs_outline: 本課程介紹財金與資訊科技整合的知識領域，呼應近期金融科技(financial technology, FinTech)在金融市場和金融機構的運用。此課程首先簡介金融產業，包括銀行、保險、證券，再依科技對金融產業的影響分為數個子題來討論，包括區塊鏈應用、機器人理財、金融大數據、人工智慧金融應用。在每個金融科技領域，本課程將介紹傳統的金融營運模式、科技的內容、來自新科技的衝擊、新種營運模式、對市場的影響、和金融機構的反應。課程內容涵蓋金融產業的領域知識及其數位化轉型方式及內涵。修課學生可以了解金融科技在金融領域的實質範疇和功能角色，以及實際運作方式和未來發展潛力。

crs_outline: Some complicated data involving relationships can be represented as a graph that consists of nodes and edges between nodes. Such graphs can serve as a fundamental tool for modeling social, technological, and biological systems. This course focuses on the computational, algorithmic, and modeling challenges specific to the analysis of massive graphs. By means of studying the underlying graph structure and its features, students are introduced to machine learning techniques and data mining tools that can help us to reveal insights into a variety of networks. We will focus on representation learning and Graph Neural Networks. Furthermore, we will cover algorithms for the World Wide Web, influence maximization, disease outbreak detection, and social network analysis.

crs_outline:
1.  This is the class about the valuation of an investment project or a company.
2.  The course first reviews the traditional discounted-cash-flow (DCF) or net-present-value (NPV) methods. 
3.  This class then introduces some real-options concepts to value an investment project or a company. This new approach is called an expanded NPV method.
4.  Finally, some basic game-theory concepts will be further employed into the expanded NPV method to consider the strategic action by competitors.
5.  By introducing lots of numerical examples, practical cases and applications, this course will train students and provide them the ability to value an investment project or a company by themselves.
6. Lecture will be provided in Chinese.

crs_outline:
This course offers an introduction to machine learning from a statistical perspective, with a strong emphasis on applications in Financial Technology (FinTech), including credit risk modeling, wealth management, and fraud detection. Students will engage in hands-on projects—shared via GitHub—that integrate theoretical concepts with practical programming. The course centers on solving real-world problems in FinTech, encouraging collaboration, innovation, and data-driven decision-making.

In addition to technical skills, students will enhance their oral presentation abilities and learn to leverage tools like ChatGPT to improve their coding and writing. Team projects will focus on key FinTech applications such as credit scoring, fraud detection, factor investing in Taiwan’s stock market, and cryptocurrency trading.

To facilitate the course, students are required to:
1) Bring a laptop to every lecture.
2) Create free accounts on the following platforms: GitHub, Overleaf, and Microsoft Teams (using their NYCU accounts).

crs_outline:
本課程教主要教授人工智慧、機器學習的理論與實務，並延伸至深度學習的基礎知識，包含Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) 和 Long-short term memory network (LSTM)等的架構與實作教學，此外對於近年來蓬勃發展的金融科技領域，也將從資財系的觀點提供資工、資管、財金或其他相關科系的研究生，踏入CS+Finance跨領域學習的必備基礎，這門課程將包含大量的Python程式實作，也會在金融投資、衍生性商品訂價、電腦視覺、數據資料分析多個實務應用中，藉由上機實作教學、課堂程式作業、小組合作專題、報告與討論各種方式，讓所有學生具備跨足人工智慧、機器學習、金融科技等所需的資訊技術與應用領域知識，課程內容包含：
1.	機器學習理論：以人工智慧、統計理論實作、樣型辨識模型與機器學習理論相關的知識為主，概述各種演算法，諸如：Concept Learning、Decision Tree、Artificial Neural Networks、Genetic Algorithms、Support Vector Machines、Instance-based Learning、Clustering Analysis、AdaBoost algorithm
2.	實例應用系統開發：在大數據分析及決策的各種跨領域應用中，以多媒體與財務資料庫較易取得，故依修課同學背景分成多媒體系統決策與財務投資決策兩組，多媒體組以大量影像、聲音、影片資訊為研究標的，探討諸如人臉偵測、人臉辨識、智慧人機互動、人體姿勢模型等先進智慧型影像識別技術及其應用。而財務投資決策則將所學之人工智慧與機器學習理論，應用於財務時間序列中，並藉此探討各種創新金融與財務管理議題。
本課程除了學習人工智慧與深度學習理論，另藉由實例應用開發來建構同學們實作的能力。此外，雙應用主題的課程設計將有效協助不同研究背景的同學，快速達到學以致用的目的。期望能將各種已經成熟的AI科技，推展至各種管理決策與產品創新應用的電腦化與智慧化。

The course will lead students into two main areas which must be analyzed in order to formulate and implement a well-conceived strategy: the external environment of the firm (the industry context), and the internal environment of the firm (its resources and capabilities). Some of the key topics covered include: (1) exploring why and how good strategic management increases business performance, (2) the application of a set of analytical frameworks, (3) analyzing the reasons for the success and failure of a firm, and (4) the methods of developing an effective competitive strategy and executing it competently. The teaching materials include lectures, case analyses, and independent readings.

We would like to introduce the framework of Logistics and Supply Chain Management in this course. Especially, we will focus on the Inbound and Operations Logistics. The students are expected to learn the long-run production/operations logistics management (production/operations planning and master production schedule), the middle-run production/operations logistics management (material requirement planning and capacity requirement planning), the short-run production/operations logistics management (shop-floor control, order release and operations scheduling), and Inbound Logistics (procurement management and subcontract management). Also, we will use the business processes of an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) information system to introduce the practice of production/operations logistics and inbound logistics.

面對未來以永續淨零、氣候變遷與調適為主要目標之國家與都市發展，軌道運輸已然成為核心基礎建設之一。軌道運輸結合管理、工程、科技等跨領域特性，以及公共運輸本身與民生和人息息相關之重要性，因此其基礎知識不可或缺。同時，軌道運輸也連結著地區經濟發展、在地居民生活文化、以及周遭的歷史、地理、與社會人文變遷，因此學習軌道運輸不管是對在運輸科技、地方發展、經濟、社會與人文方面的了解都相當重要。本課程在於使學生了解軌道運輸系統在城際運輸系統及都市運輸系統中的重要性，並就軌道系統中的子系統如車輛、設施、號誌、供電的運作及其界面進行介紹。本課程強調軌道運輸安全之重要性，並會介紹軌道運輸安全管理系統。此外本課程亦介紹各種軌道系統如高鐵、傳統鐵路、捷運及輕軌系統之差異性及適用性。本課程亦會探討軌道系統規劃、建設、營運、維修、及組織改革等不同課題並提供實務經驗。本課程將簡述軌道運輸與城市發展、地方經濟、社會人文之關係與影響。

In light of the future national and urban development with sustainable net zero, climate change and adaptation as the main goals, rail transportation has become one of the core infrastructure. Rail transportation combines the cross-disciplinary characteristics of management, engineering, technology, and the importance of public transportation itself to people's livelihood and people, so its basic knowledge is indispensable. At the same time, rail transportation is also linked to regional economic development, local residents' living culture, and the surrounding history, geography, and social and cultural changes. Therefore, learning rail transportation is very important for understanding transportation technology, local development, economy, society and humanities. This course aims to enable students to understand the importance of rail transportation systems in intercity transportation systems and urban transportation systems, and introduce the operation and interface of subsystems in rail systems such as vehicles, facilities, signals, and power supply. This course emphasizes the importance of rail transportation safety and will introduce rail transportation safety management systems. In addition, this course also introduces the differences and applicability of various rail systems such as high-speed rail, traditional railways, metro and light rail systems. This course will also explore different topics such as rail system planning, construction, operation, maintenance, and organizational reform and provide practical experience. This course will briefly describe the relationship and impact of rail transportation on urban development, local economy, and social humanities.

The Intended Learning Outcomes (ILOs) of this class are:
1. Understand different types of railway systems
2. Identify key characteristics of rail transportation and its advantages and disadvantages compared to other transportation modes. 
3. Understand main functions and characteristics of rail infrastructure.
4. Understand main functions and characteristics of rail rolling stock.
5. Understand main functions and characteristics of rail power and resistance.
6. Understand main functions and characteristics of rail train control and signaling systems.
7. Learn practical management experiences in the planning, construction, and operation of railway system.

捷運系統（metro system）在都會大眾運輸當中提供安全、快捷、且高效率之運輸服務。不同於傳統鐵路運輸系統，捷運系統具有站距短、班次密集、列車加減速快、營運時間長等特性，這些特性讓捷運系統之營運、維護保養、與管理有著獨特的挑戰與技術需求。本課程將介紹捷運系統之營運與管理，並著重在其於實務上之應用。本課程建立於基礎軌道運輸知識之上，介紹捷運系統之系統架構以及各子系統（設施、車輛、號誌、行車控制、車站等）之功能、關聯、與特色。本課程將進一步與國內捷運公司合作，重點介紹列車特性、基礎營運規劃、行車控制、與維修保養，並且將透過現地參訪方式，讓學生對於捷運系統實務有更深入之認識。本課程連結捷運系統之知識與國內捷運系統實務，旨在讓學生更進一步學習國內捷運系統營運之具體狀況，讓學生能夠具備銜接軌道運輸系統與管理理論與實務營運之能力，培養捷運運輸產業之知能與技術基礎。

Metro systems provide safe, fast, and efficient transportation services in urban public transport. Unlike traditional railway systems, metro systems are characterized by short station spacing, frequent service, rapid train acceleration and deceleration, and long operating hours. These characteristics present unique challenges and technical requirements for the operation, maintenance, and management of metro systems. This course will introduce the operation and management of metro systems, focusing on their practical applications. Building upon basic railway transportation knowledge, this course introduces the metro systems framework and the functions, relationships, and characteristics of subsystems (facilities, rolling stock, signaling, train control, stations, etc.). Collaborating with domestic metro companies, this course will further introduce metro train characteristics, basic operational planning, train control, and maintenance, and will include site visits to provide students with a deeper understanding of metro system practices. This course connects knowledge of the metro system with the practical aspects of the domestic metro system, aiming to enable students to further learn about the specific operation of the domestic metro system, and to equip them with the ability to connect the management theory and practical operation of rail transit systems, thereby cultivating their knowledge and technical foundation in the metro transportation industry.

Class Description:
This course introduces the fundamental concepts and facts of chemistry. Students will learn to apply knowledge gained from observing and exploring the nature of substances and their changes, enabling them to control these changes and create various new substances.

Indented Learning Outcomes: 
1. Explore the Nature of Science: Learn to use scientific methods to understand the world.
2. Demonstrate the Importance and Characteristics of Chemistry: Discover how chemistry impacts our daily lives.
3. Develop Problem-Solving Skills: Utilize knowledge to address new and unforeseen problems. Learn to deconstruct complex, challenging issues into manageable, simple components.
4. Enhance Conceptual Understanding of Chemical Principles: Describe phenomena with a deep conceptual understanding beyond just applying a set of rules.

This class will be taught in English.

crs_outline: 在課程中提供分析化學的知識、背景及重要的基本原理﹐並搭配實機講解使同學熟悉分析化學的背景知識與儀器設計及操作. 另外, 在取得樣品時﹐懂得如何應用所習得的知識選擇適當的儀器進行量測,以及在取得量測數據後,如何進行分析與評估. 在課程主題部分包含統計學、資料處理分析、光譜學(包含旋光光譜)、層析法顯微影像技術，並針對生物分子分析技術之進行介紹. This course will introduce fundamental concepts of analytical chemistry, focusing on the approaches relevant to measurements in biochemistry and light-matter interactions. Topics include error analysis, statistical treatment of data, spectroscopy, thermal analysis, chromatography analysis, and the introduction of optical microscopy.

crs_outline: 拉丁文原自羅馬帝國，也是歐洲各語系源頭之一，中古世紀，拉丁文是全歐洲通用的語言，生物醫學在過去拉丁文也曾是主要的使用語言之一．例如“De humani corporis fabrica”即是以拉丁文撰寫的人體解剖學的權威著作之一。本課程開課的初衷在於，過往觀察到學生在學習生物醫學的專業過程中，專有名詞往往是最大障礙，若能先學會拉丁文的發音，名詞，形容詞，動詞以及相關基礎文法，在搭配引進基礎與應用之生物醫學的拉丁文專有名詞及應答等,讓同學能有更穩固的基礎後，能更容易理解與掌握後續的基礎與應用生物醫學等專業課目．

cos_cname: 程式設計 Go Go Go
dep_ename: Department of Biological Science and Technology
crs_outline:
(本文作者為陽明交通大學羅惟正，保留智慧財產權。摘錄請註明出處。)

1. 講授主題：Go 程式設計。
Go 是 Google 開發的平行運算式程式語言，有兩個通行版本：官方編譯器版 (Golang Compiler version) 及自由軟體編譯器版 (GNU Compiler Collection version)。本課程採用官方版本，"Go Go Go" 為 Google Golang-compiler Go 之簡稱。

Go 可用極簡程式碼完成複雜平行運算，而大數據時代，各領域的龐大運算量(如人工智慧演算)仰賴優異的平行運算系統。因此，Go 在 2016 被軟體評價公司 TIOBE 評選為年度最佳程式語言。


2. 課程宗旨：推廣高效能平行運算科技。
我們相信，臺灣絕對有實力在科技舞台引領國際。程式教育之普及、量子平行運算之深研，必有助臺灣在資訊科技領域搶佔全球C位。本課程旨在推廣平行運算程式教育，期待新時代學子以資訊知能為跨領域融合的共同語言，開發新穎量子運算技術，推動臺灣在數位崛起之路彎道超車，成為科技領頭羊。


3. 開設理念與目標
量子平行運算，是即將顛覆人類文明、商機遠勝當前AI的重大科技。我們的理念，是以平行運算程式教育為臺灣培育優秀的量子運算人才，搶在全球之先，掌握量子運算科技。具體目標為：

(1)以Golang為主題，讓學員熟稔平行運算程式語言。
(2)以量子運算熱門題綱設計作業，為學員儲備量子演算法開發所需基礎知識。
(3)以Golang與CUDA的連結為進階實作，使學員有能力操控現代高階平行運算設備，為未來操作量子電腦預做技術準備。


4. 程式教育願景概述
近年，因網路科技進步及可攜式計算機普及，全球邁入數位時代，諸國競相崛起。偏偏，臺灣因資訊科技發展早，導致年輕學子雖是數位時代原住民，卻普遍不覺得資訊科技新鮮、值得掌握。羅老師多年從事跨領域程式教育，發現學子們對程式設計的興向有分化之勢。極端化的發展，導致部份學生極力擠進資、通、電子、電機等程式能力得以直接應用之領域，其他學生的人生發展則與程式語言不易結緣。

第一類人才，掌握了程式與資通電機等專業技能，但對社會經濟文化等領域較陌生；第二類人才則由於不了解程式語言，不易想像資通電機科技如何幫助自身領域之發展。跨領域科技研發，固然能靠團隊協作，但背景各異的人才的不同思維模式，常形成溝通障礙。此時，熟悉雙方思維與基礎知能的兩棲型人才，便能為跨域整合發揮極大助力。

千禧年初電腦與網路普及化時期，許多不擅長電腦操作的人成了被推倒的前浪。而今新世代學子一出生便有電腦與人工智慧相伴，可謂無電腦文盲。值此數位科技普及化時期，想控制電腦與人工智慧而非被其取代，須具備的基本能力是看得懂程式語言。換言之，在數位時代，「程式文盲」很可能成為下一波沙灘上的前浪。

本課程期盼憑藉理工生醫人社等背景的學生都易學易懂的程式設計教材，為社會培育新世代的兩棲型跨領域領導人才，期許他們充分應用程式語言之優勢，掌握、甚至引領時代趨勢，協助福爾摩沙重歸數位科技與科技金融巨頭之林。


5. 量子運算願景概述
量子運算是以量子位元架構成量子電腦所進行的運算，量子運算基於量子力學的疊加態與糾纏態，為天然的高效能平行運算。在合適主題上，速度可以是傳統電腦的數百萬乃至數億倍快。目前，全球科技大國與頂尖企業如 Google, IBM, Microsoft 與 Intel 等，都在競相研發量子電腦。

人工智慧系統仰賴平行運算處理海量資訊。目前的人工智慧，由於硬體瓶頸，不得不用高度簡化、將大量細節資訊捨棄的演算方式來運作，性能雖已相當驚豔，且加速了各產業之發展，但終究難有真正的自主思考能力與創造力。量子電腦發展穩定後，若以量子運算重構人工智慧演算法，真正有意識的人造智慧體，很可能因此誕生。爾後，人類文明將迎向科技大爆炸的奇異點，所有產業將以難以言喻的超高速度發展。

當今，誰能掌握量子運算科技，便掌握了未來科技與產業發展的話語權。量子運算是天然高效能平行運算，而 Go 是當前最強大的平行運算程式語言。本課程搭配後續課程「Go人工智慧大數據平行運算」及「分散運算式網頁程式設計」，將以 Go 為經、量子運算為緯，訓練高效能平行運算演算法開發人才，為臺灣在全球量子運算科技爭霸之路上，預先培育優秀的種子人才。

crs_outline:
在發展現代生物科學及將其轉化成科技產業的過程中，數學分析是不可或缺的工具．本課程將介紹常用數值解析的原理與方法，並訓練用 Matlab 軟體解決問題的能力．應用以生科相關問題為主，介紹如何利用數學方法解析生物系統．由於數學解析為各類科技產業的共同根基，本課程也將增進學生追求跨領域生涯的能力．

This course introduces the principles and practices of commonly used numerical methods and how to use them in Matlab to solve problems requiring mathematical analysis.

crs_outline: 生技醫療產品幾乎與人體健康有著直接的關係，所以全球各個國家地區在法律上皆有嚴格的規範，多數此類產品必須取得當地特定的證照才能生產或銷售。加上全球對於環境保護的意識加重，永續(ESG)亦成為重要課題。本課程將針對化妝品，醫療器材，藥品，保健食品等的規範，以及永續管理，向同學做蓋括性的介紹，為了使同學將來進入職場時，可以快速接軌產業需求。

crs_outline:
This course covers the principles of mass spectrometry and proteomics, along with their applications in life sciences, biomedical research, and clinical studies. Students will learn the fundamentals of protein identification and characterization using modern mass spectrometry-based technologies.

The course includes flipped-classroom activities and hands-on laboratory sessions (subject to enrollment), providing opportunities for students to gain practical experience in experimental design, laboratory techniques, data interpretation, and scientific communication.

Students interested in proteomics, mass spectrometry, or related research fields are encouraged to enroll, particularly those who anticipate using these technologies in their future research projects.

此堂課主要教導質譜儀原理、蛋白質體技術基本原理、與其實際應用範圍與臨床應用。 
本學期加入翻轉教室課程及部分實際操作(將視選課人數有所修正)，希望讓學生能有實際體驗實驗操作、實驗設計、與成果報告。 歡迎想學習、或實驗會接觸到蛋白體或質譜分析的學生選課。

dep_ename: Department of Biological Science and Technology
crs_outline:
課程概述與目標：
概論光電元件於生物物理實用技術,並介紹如何將這些技術實際運用於現代分子和細胞生物物理和生物化學研究◦內容包括:幾何光學、光學元件原理與應用、常見用於生物物理實驗之電子儀器與應用實例◦

This course will provide fundamental concepts on optical and electrical techniques in biophysics. Those techniques are general used to study the structure and function of biological macromolecules. The goal of this course is to help students to develop physical understanding about daily-used instruments in biophysical and biochemistry laboratory.

dep_ename: Department of Biological Science and Technology
crs_outline: 本課程為生物科技學院「實驗動物模式模組化課程」之一，將介紹常見實驗動物(包括囓齒類、兔形目、貓、狗、有蹄類、非人類靈長類等)，在解剖、生理、遺傳、行為等方面的特性，讓學生對於個別實驗動物的命名、飼養、管理、環境等要求及相關規範有基本認識，並瞭解這些實驗動物在科學領域的應用及對人類的貢獻。而提供實驗動物穩定的生活環境以及優良的獸醫照護(動物運送、隔離、臨床觀察、健康監測等)，對於確保動物實驗品質、增進動物福祉、與對動物實驗的影響層面也是本課程的重點，期望在具備這些知識後，能幫助學生建立面對實驗動物的正確態度及觀念，藉以將動物實驗的誤差減到最小。

cos_cname: 實驗動物3R倫理原則與技術實作
memo: 上課地點：博愛校區實驗動物中心2樓-3R智慧教室。
cos_ename: 3Rs Principles and Practical Techniques in Laboratory Animal Experiments
dep_ename: Department of Biological Science and Technology
crs_outline:
由於實驗動物對人類生活各層面的貢獻以及其對生物醫學研究領域的重要性已無庸置疑，而當使用實驗動物已成不可避免的趨勢之時，如何合理使用、善待實驗動物、使其承受最少的傷害與痛苦，以確保實驗動物有優良的生活品質及人道的結束生命，是「動物保護法」尊重動物生命及保護動物的核心精神，也是近年來行政院農業委員會管理實驗動物使用、強調動物福祉的主要依據。
本課程為生物科技學院「實驗動物模式模組化課程」之一，前半部份將介紹動物福祉及動物權的核心觀念與其歷史演進，探討在兼顧動物實驗的品質與動物福祉的情況下，如何確保實驗動物能有優良的生活品質及人道的結束生命，包含在設計動物實驗時應掌握的替代(Replacement)、減量(Reduction)、精緻化(Refinement) 3R原則，以及在實驗進行中使動物免於饑渴、免於恐懼、免於身體不適、免於痛苦傷害和疾病、表現自然行為等五大自由(5 Freedom)，並介紹動物保護法對實驗動物相關的法規規範，以避免違反動物福祉事件的發生，進而幫助學生建立面對實驗動物時尊重生命(Respect)及負責任(Responsibility)的正確態度及觀念。另一方面，精進實驗動物操作技術是研究人員重視動物福祉的積極具體展現之一，本課程後半部份的實習操作，讓學生親自操作麻醉、手術、評估疼痛、人道終點時機、並進行安樂死等，期望使學生具備及熟習實驗動物的基本操作技術，並加深其對於動物實驗及動物福址的體會。

crs_outline:
隨著後基因體時代來臨，生物學家開始嘗試從基因體/蛋白質層次到生物網路層次去解析複雜的細胞行為。本課程包括介紹如何建構複雜生物網絡，以及介紹當代網絡生物學和系統生物學中使用的統計方法和數據集成，主要內容如下：
（1）如何處理來自基因調控，蛋白質—蛋白質相互作用，蛋白質複合物/模組之原始數據，包括數據處理、聚類、功能富集分析和生物網路之建立。
（2）介紹網路理論和網路模型的基礎知識。
（3）實例說明如何將基因體/蛋白質體數據用於網路重建、結合和驗證；以及如何透過這些生物網路探討疾病機制及辨識生物標記。


In the post-genomic era, biologists started to try to resolve complex cellular behaviors from the genomic/proteomic level to the biological network level. This course covers the process of reconstructing complex biological networks and the introduction of statistical methods and data integration used in contemporary network biology and systems biology as follows.
(1) The tutorials for processing raw data from gene regulation, protein-protein interactions, protein complexes/modules, including data processing, clustering, and enrichment analysis, and network establishment.
(2) The fundamentals of network theory and network models
(3) The examples of how genomic/proteomic data are used for biological network reconstruction, integration, and validation, as well as how to use these biological networks for exploring disease mechanisms and identifying biomarkers.

cos_cname: 分散運算式網頁伺服器設計
cos_ename: Distributed Computation and its Practice in Web Servers
dep_ename: Department of Biological Science and Technology
crs_outline:
課程性質：編譯式中高階程式語言之平行運算網路程式設計教學與實作
本課程以C語言為核心，建立學生的高效能運算與系統開發能力，並銜接量子運算與分散式網路通訊的技術脈動。

講授主題：C平行運算與網頁伺服器設計
C是歷久彌新的中階程式語言，許多現代語言如 C++、PHP、Python 與 Golang 都是以它所開發。然而，C語言在跨平台與學習曲線上具備不小挑戰。本課程結合新世代Clang編譯器與教師自行開發的函式庫進行教學，提升跨平台實作效率並降低入門門檻。課程進一步結合平行運算與網路通訊兩大主題，帶領學生以C語言開發多核心平行處理程式，並實作具備多連線應答能力的網頁伺服器。

核心目標：連結程式設計能力與平行運算趨勢
隨著行動裝置普及與科技演進，全球資訊量呈爆炸性成長，推動社會進入大數據時代並促進人工智慧發展。大數據分析與人工智慧皆仰賴高效能平行運算，同時，現代科研及產業應用幾乎都以網路通訊為媒介。本課程期望使學生同時掌握這兩大能力，在數位轉型和科技創新浪潮中，具備關鍵競爭力。

前瞻展望：從GPU到量子平行運算
平行運算的極致技術形態是量子運算。量子位元可透過疊加與糾纏態同時攜帶多重資訊，使量子運算在合適主題上能展現超越傳統運算百萬倍以上的速度，商機凌駕當前AI。各資訊科技大國及 Google, IBM, Microsoft, Intel 等頂尖企業均投入量子電腦研發，可見其戰略地位。

在量子電腦成熟前，我們預期量子晶片將率先以類似GPU的加速器形式問世。而目前主流GPU計算語言即為C語言。具備C語言平行運算實作能力的學生，將最有潛力銜接未來量子運算的實務應用。

課程願景
量子運算正逐步走出實驗室的幽暗，迎向實用化的曙光，這場技術革命將深刻改寫人類科技文明與商業型態。我們相信，學生若及早投入，不僅能強化職涯競爭力與收入，更將在未來的科技與產業版圖中掌握主動權。本課程期望啟發學生以長遠視野看待自身於新時代中的角色，以專業知能積極貢獻社會、協助臺灣提升國際影響力，引領人們穿越科技奇異點，成為推動下一場文明飛躍的創新領導者。

本課程之授課教師具備醫學影像與動物實驗之專業背景，擁有國家醫事放射師執照，並具有臨床與研究經驗，長期運用非侵入性影像進行動物疾病評估、治療與縱向追蹤，並具備臨床與前臨床整合之轉譯研究經驗。
課程將介紹X光、電腦斷層、磁振造影與超音波等生醫影像技術之基本原理，每種影像皆涵蓋人體與實驗動物之影像判讀。內容包含影像技術由結構顯影發展至功能與分子層次之應用，結合顯影劑與生物標靶以提升疾病診斷能力，並作為連結臨床醫學與實驗動物研究的重要工具，提供疾病模型建立、治療評估與長期追蹤之非侵入性資訊。在此基礎上，課程將進一步說明影像技術於3Rs principle（Reduction, Refinement）中的應用，包括透過非侵入性與縱向影像追蹤降低動物使用數量（Reduction），以及減少侵入性操作與動物負擔（Refinement），並藉由臨床與動物影像資料之整合，提升研究效率與實驗設計品質。
學生將理解生醫影像之成像原理，學習辨識不同影像模態並進行初步判讀，並培養其在規劃實驗動物研究時，能運用影像技術設計符合3R原則之研究策略。課程將結合講授、小組討論與實作，並以小劇場呈現學習成果。

costype: 領域課程-社會中的科技與自然
crs_outline:
課程概述與目標：
I. 課程概述
本課程為英語授課課程
普通生物學（一）為生物科技學系之基礎課程，為本系學生選修未來進階課程的基礎。本課程涵蓋的範圍包括化學生物學、細胞生物學、遺傳學與分子生物學的基本知識。 在生物化學部分，介紹生物巨分子與基礎代謝作用。 細胞生物學方面，著重於胞器功能，訊號傳遞與細胞分裂。 遺傳學方面，則由古典之孟德爾遺傳學，果蠅遺傳學到近代遺傳學。分子生物學部分，著重於中心法則中之轉錄與轉譯，並延伸至生物科技的介紹與應用。

II. 學習目標
   完成本課程後，學生應具備下列能力：
   1.	建立對專業學科的基礎知識：
	a. 描述生物巨分子之功能，基本代謝作用，訊號傳遞路徑，細胞分裂與細胞週期，中心法則之調控機制
	b. 分析遺傳特性並計算性狀之遺傳概率
	c. 區分真核與原核生物間中心法則調控上之異同
	d. 分析生物科技應用時的倫理困境與其解方
   2.	使用英文為學習工具
	a. 增進原文課本之閱讀
	b. 使用英文進行課堂發表
	c. 使用英文撰寫作業與學期報告
	d. 使用英語專有名詞

III. 學習活動
為達成學習目標，本課程之學習活動如下：
1.	教師授課： 教師根據課本製作投影片等教材進行直接授課
2.	團隊學習： 自趙老師部分開始，進行小組活動，學生須分組，並以小組為單位進行小組學習，完成課堂間小組討論，小組上台發表，課後小組作業，與學期末之小組書面報告撰寫。除小組討論時學生可用母語進行討論外，其他活動主要由英文進行，母語為輔助。
	
IV. 注意事項
  1. 為維護本系學生(含雙主修/輔系/跨域學程學生)修課權益，第一.二階段僅階段性開放人數20名， 第三階段開學後開放加選。
  2. 本課程為生物科技系一年級的基礎必修課，會以生物科技系必修的標準來上課以及評分。
  3. 開放外系同學選修作為通識，目的是讓同學的學識能加廣，有機會做跨領域的學習與研究。提醒選修本課程作為通識學分的同學，做好需要認真上課、念書的心理準備；請有決心的同學再加選
  4. 本課程有小組活動與作業，若不願意負責地投入小組活動共同學習的同學請勿選修 （不負責的同學在小組活動部分無法獲得成績）
  5. 由於後2/3學期每週皆有課堂小組討論，無法準時到課偏好在家自學的同學請勿選修。
  6. 課程內容與要求會隨課程人數修正，教師擁有開學後修改課程內容與要求之權利，請同學注意開學時的各項公告與課程資料以掌握最新資訊
Course Overview and Objectives

I. Course Overview
This course is conducted in English.General Biology (I) is a foundational course for students in the Department of Biotechnology and serves as a prerequisite for more advanced courses in the field. The course content covers basic knowledge in chemical biology, cell biology, genetics, and molecular biology.
* In the biochemistry section, the course introduces biological macromolecules and basic metabolic processes.
* In cell biology, the focus is on organelle functions, signal transduction, and cell division.
* In genetics, the course covers classical Mendelian genetics, Drosophila genetics, and modern genetics.
* The molecular biology portion emphasizes transcription and translation within the central dogma, and extends to the introduction and application of biotechnology.

II. Learning Objectives
Upon successful completion of the course, students should be able to:
1. Establish foundational knowledge in the discipline:
    a. Describe the functions of biological macromolecules, basic metabolic processes, signal transduction pathways, cell division and the cell cycle, and regulatory mechanisms within the central dogma.
    b. Analyze genetic traits and calculate probabilities of trait inheritance.
    c. Differentiate the regulatory mechanisms of the central dogma between eukaryotes and prokaryotes.
    d. Evaluate ethical dilemmas in the application of biotechnology and propose solutions.
2. Use English as a learning tool:
    a. Improve the ability to read English-language textbooks.
    b. Deliver class presentations in English.
    c. Write assignments and term reports in English.
    d. Use English scientific terminology.

III. Learning Activities
To achieve the learning objectives, the following activities will be implemented:
1. Instructor Lectures:The instructor will deliver lectures based on the textbook and prepare teaching materials such as slides.
2. Team-Based Learning:Beginning from the portion taught by Professor Chao, students will participate in group activities. These include in-class group discussions, group presentations, group assignments, and a final written group report.While students may use their native language for group discussions, all other activities will be primarily conducted in English, with the native language used only as a supplement.

IV. Notes
1. To protect the enrollment rights of students in the Department of Biotechnology (including double majors, minors, and interdisciplinary program students), the number of spots will be limited to 20 during the first two enrollment phases. Additional enrollment will be opened during the third phase after the semester begins.
2. This is a required foundational course for first-year students in the Department of Biotechnology. It will be taught and graded according to the standards for department majors.
3. Students from other departments are welcome to take this course as a general education elective, providing them an opportunity to broaden their academic knowledge and engage in interdisciplinary learning and research. Students intending to take the course for general education credit should be prepared to attend class seriously and study diligently. Only those with such commitment should register.
4. This course involves group activities and assignments. Students who are unwilling to participate responsibly in collaborative learning should not enroll. (Students who do not contribute to group activities will not receive grades for that component.)
5. The last two-thirds of the semester will include weekly in-class group discussions. Students who prefer to study independently at home or who cannot attend class on time should not enroll.
6. Course content and requirements may be adjusted based on enrollment size. The instructor reserves the right to modify course content and requirements after the semester begins. Students should pay attention to announcements and course materials at the beginning of the semester to stay informed of the latest updates.

crs_outline:
建築是文化與生活的集結表現，是個體與社會之間的媒合，人與自然的中介，也是藝術與工程間的巧妙交會。
「建築概論」課程主旨不在於介紹個別建築物或建築師，而在於建立對整體建築環境的觀點與認識，分為其下幾個主題： 
 
（一）個人觀點的建築：身體、空間、居住 
（二）物質觀點的建築：結構、構築、設計 
（三）社會觀點的建築：類型、發展、時代 

課程以主題分享講授為主，另外安排影片觀賞或邀請演講等方式進行，並強調線上小組討論，與課後直接問答回應，目標在於培養對於空間狀況的思辨能力，能以科學、技術、政治經濟、社會文化等多重角度理解建築的複雜意義。

crs_outline:
近年電腦輔助設計與電腦輔助製造開啟突破性的新紀元，逐漸打破設計、加工與製造的藩籬，跨領域應用金工的案例也顯著增加。本課程以跨領域金屬應用為核心，探索材料特性、材料的構造詩性 (Tectonic)、數位工具應用與設計實作能力。

本課程以漸進的方式建構金工與數位工具實作能力，分為三個單元：
前置練習: 金工基礎與設計複習
本單元以少量案例帶領學生複習金工核心工法，包括鋸、磨、焊、拋等基本技術，並重新建立對金屬材料特性、工具設備操作與安全規範的理解。此階段亦將介紹課程中將使用的多種金屬材料，協助學生調整手感並銜接後續的數位製造流程。

〔單元一〕 數位製造Part 1.與複合媒材應用
課程將帶領同學由淺入深掌握 3D 繪圖軟體 Rhino 的核心能力。第一單元從軟體介面導覽、基本操作到精確製圖，循序建立扎實基礎；並進一步認識「點、線」及其相關編輯技巧，讓同學能獨立完成各類圖形建構，為後續的數位製造與進階創作奠定穩固根基。

在本單元中，課程也將實際運用多種數位製造工具，包括金屬雷射切割、壓克力與紙材、木材的雷射加工，並搭配異材質冷接技法，拓展金屬與複合媒材的創作可能性。此單元更與工學院機械實習工場合作，由實習工場專業師資帶領 1–2 堂課，進行雷射製造的理論講解、實務見習與安全操作講習，讓同學在真實設備環境中累積寶貴經驗。

〔單元二〕 數位製造 Part 2.與金屬鑄造
承接單元一的平面建構基礎，單元二將帶領同學進一步進入立體造形與幾何思維的世界。課程將運用 3D 列印與 3D 純蠟列印，並結合翻砂鑄造與脫蠟鑄造等金屬成形技術，讓同學在從數位模型逐步推進至實體作品的製作過程中，系統性理解立體結構的建構原理，掌握材料在成形階段所展現的可塑性，並進一步認識不同製程所帶來的造形可能與技術特性。

金屬材料本身擁有豐富而迷人的表情；從硬度、延展性到化學反應（如氧化、銅綠、染色），每一種金屬都展現獨特的質地與語彙。同學們將透過認識、比較與實作，學習如何選擇、混合與轉化不同金屬，進而在創作中探索材料的「構造詩性」，讓作品不僅在形式上完整，也能展現深層的材料語言與創作思維。

〔單元三〕設計與實踐
第三單元將進入分組或個人設計發想與執行階段，整合跨領域不同專長之核心技能以課程命題進行發想、討論、設計並實際製作。

特別提醒：金工實作並非一蹴而得，在設計製作上需要投入一定的時間與心力！同學們平均每週需額外花 3~6 小時以上準備設計與作業，期中期末作品製作尤費時間請務必審慎斟酌個人所能投入的時間
※ 本課程有別於一般選修與通識課程形式，授課、討論、工作坊形式穿插進行，將在學期第一堂課與同學們討論課程時數調配
※ 本課程將於各階段安排練習與作業，於期中、期末各安排一次作品會審並於校館展示一週

crs_outline:
當今任一種⾵格的調性音樂創作，和弦連接變化時常作為進行時基礎動⼒之一。本堂「和聲學」即是專注討論⾳⾼組織在縱向與橫向交互關係的系統。調性和聲在⼗九世紀歐洲音樂中有成熟的發展，作曲家們互相影響、彼此切磋分享創作的技術，形成⼀股聽覺上的美學脈絡，至今眾多學者整理成系統研究，探討⾳階中橫向的動⾳與靜⾳，其中以「導⾳音向上解決」為最重要核⼼，進而延伸出更複雜的縱向三和弦與屬七和弦連接，在以四聲部織度體與⼤⼩調七聲音階架構下，透視不和諧與和諧之間的交互作用。

本堂「和聲學（一）」著重在調內的和聲進行，「和聲學（二）」將探討更多半音變化、轉調、混合調式等用法。

costype: 領域課程-社會中的科技與自然
crs_outline:
面對當代自然環境及社會環境的快速變遷，人類賴以生存的都市空間正面臨具大的挑戰。在尋求創意及永續的發展過程中，必須先理解城當代市發展以及社會環境變化，而後透過創新的方法進行分析甚至進行設計規劃。永續發展不只是一個指標或議題，更是當代急迫需要解決的問題，自然生態及人類文明的發展不應該是對抗或相互矛盾的選擇，如何透過創意建立共存、共生、共榮的可能性，成為課程最重要的目標。

本課程共分為七大主題，包含城市意象、創意城市、智慧城市、藝術城市、城市創生、循環城市、永續生態。循序漸進從城市的觀察方法進入當代城市的設計方法，從科技發展到社會應用層面，最終形塑自然生態及人類文明共同永續發展的樣貌。

dep_ename: Department of Biological Science and Technology
crs_outline:
Class Description:
“Microbial Genetic Engineering " is a comprehensive, hands-on course designed to guide students through the fundamental techniques employed in the rapidly evolving fields of Genetic Engineering. The course covers a range of topics including plasmid construction,  gene expression manipulation, bacterial host genomic modifications, enzyme bioprospecting,  enzyme assay and pathway assay, protein engineering and direct evolution, and an introduction to the latest sequencing technologies. Through real-world examples, students will learn how to design, conduct, and interpret experimental results, and gain a deeper understanding of the practical aspects of these technologies.

Purpose of the Class:
The purpose of this course is to equip students with the practical skills and knowledge in Genetic Engineering, which are essential for contributing to research and development in the fields of Metabolic Engineering and Synthetic Biology. It aims to give students a solid foundation of key techniques, encourage critical thinking, promote innovative experimental design, and foster an understanding of the practical applications of these concepts in various applications, including biotechnology, biofuel and biochemical productions, and pharmaceuticals.

This class will be taught in English.

crs_outline:
Our final goal of the course is to construct sound arguments while negotiating with others. To do so, we must understand what valid arguments consist of and what standards we are holding in our minds.   
The course is designed with three units, from foundation to application: understanding morality, examining modern laws, and practicing debate rules and tactics. We will learn fundamental theories from the founding philosophers. And then we will apply these theories to modern laws to discuss their legitimacy. By doing so, we are also seeking the metrics of our inner morality. That's how we decide on our stance. In the end, theories and our standards are put into use in debate topics, national and global.

dep_ename: Department of Foreign Languages and Literatures
crs_outline: This course is designed to cultivate students’ communication skills through the engaging format of Public Forum Debate, conducted entirely in English. Each week, students will explore current and relevant topics, developing their ability to articulate well-reasoned arguments, conduct effective research to support their claims, and listen critically to diverse perspectives. Through in-class discussions, presentations, and practice debates, students will hone their persuasive speaking techniques and master the specific structure and strategies of Public Forum Debate. The midterm assessment will evaluate their understanding and application of these principles within a full Public Forum Debate. Towards the end of the course, students will also be introduced to the fundamental concepts of Simplified Parliamentary Debate, providing a broader understanding of different debate styles and further enhancing their adaptability in spoken communication. By the conclusion of this course, students will have significantly strengthened their oral communication fluency, argumentation skills, critical thinking abilities, research capabilities, and confidence in expressing themselves persuasively and effectively in English within academic and public discourse.

dep_ename: Department of Foreign Languages and Literatures
crs_outline:
This course aims to equip students with advanced skills for communicating clear, compelling positions and arguments in writing.

Each class, we will devote time to the following activities:

Reviewing writing topics, including contemporary questions concerning the impact of LLMs (popularly known by the misnomer "AI").

Analyzing a work of art, poem, film trailer, news story (from audiovisual news source in English) and generate written arguments based on your interests and interpretations of each. This task will sometimes involve group discussion to brainstorm connections and associate themes. 
It will also become one of your homework assignments. 

Workshop (peer review) of previous week's in-class writing. (Sometimes at the beginning of the class.)
(Your in-class individual writing will be polished for peer review in the next class (and then turned in for grading in the class after that, that is, after yet further polishing.)

Review and discussion of issues in rhetoric and logic: how (not) to construct an argument: centers around how to form compelling arguments and avoid fallacies.

As time allows, other readings, including: model paragraphs and short nonfiction writing

Class assignments are usually limited to one paragraph (or about 250-300 words) to focus on a limited number of writing mistakes as well as strategies for improving sentences, transitions, diction, and paragraph structure. The aim of the course, however, is to develop coherent short essays, and will follow the conventional five-paragraph essay structure.

To develop advanced skills in argumentation, students will also construct outlines of arguments.

crs_outline:
This course offers a general introduction to linguistics, the scientific study of human language, with a focus on the sound systems of human languages. We will cover some core theoretical subfields of linguistics, namely phonetics, phonology, and morphology. We will also touch upon other subfields of linguistics, including historical linguistics, linguistic typology, and linguistic variation. This course is meant to be taken with Introduction to Linguistics II, which covers the remaining core subfields of linguistics.

Learning Outcomes:
-	Understand and refute common misconceptions about language and linguistics
-	Transcribe the consonants and vowels of English using the International Phonetic Alphabet, as well as describe their articulation 
-	Locate and describe patterns of sound distribution in data of various languages
-	Describe the structure of words and word forming processes
-	Reason about language change and language genealogy
-	Talk about the relationship between language use and social structures
-	Identify different writing systems

Course Description 
This workshop offers a practical, hands-on approach to translation, with a strong emphasis on weekly practice using articles in English-to-Chinese and Chinese-to-English directions.
Through these consistent, real-world applications, the course aims to equip students with the essential knowledge and skills vital for translators in the news industry.

Students are expected to be active participants, engaging in self-analysis, self-critique, peer reviews, and presentations to gain a comprehensive understanding of the translation process.
Additionally, we’ll explore how to leverage online applications and digital tools, including AI chatbots, to refine and enhance translated works. 
We’ll also discuss the evolving role of the translator in the digital age.
By the end of the semester, you’ll have at least 2 polished translated works (1 English-to-Chinese and 1 Chinese-to-English) ready as samples, which can be invaluable if you’re looking to pursue a career in the news industry.

To equip students with skills and knowledge of translation.
To help students develop robust problem-solving and decision-making abilities for overcoming translation challenges.
To foster a clear understanding of the professional demands and nature of a translator’s role.
To prepare students with the essential skills and adaptable strategies for working as a translator in the age of AI chatbots, including how to effectively utilize and critically engage with these technologies.

crs_outline:
This course offers an in-depth exploration of the English language, with a particular focus on its early historical development and the linguistic stages of Old English and Middle English. It examines how these earlier forms of English evolved over time and contributed to the development of modern English.
Students will study the language of the Anglo-Saxons, including its pronunciation, grammatical system, and key syntactic structures. The course gradually introduces authentic Old English and Middle English texts, enabling students to engage directly with historical language data.
Through a combination of readings, short texts, and online resources—such as the Old English Aerobics website—students will develop both a theoretical understanding of historical linguistics and practical skills in reading and analyzing early English. Particular emphasis is placed on the systematic study of grammar, including nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and word order. Students will also learn to use glossaries effectively and to interpret texts within their historical and linguistic contexts.
By the end of this course, students will be able to:
A. Identify key linguistic features of Old English and the Anglo-Saxon period.
B. Analyze Old English grammar, including inflectional morphology and syntax.
C. Read and comprehend selected Old English texts with the aid of glossaries and translations.
D. Apply grammatical knowledge to analyze and interpret Old English passages.
E. Identify key linguistic features of Middle English.
F. Analyze Middle English grammar, including inflectional morphology and syntax.
G. Apply grammatical knowledge to analyze and interpret Middle English passages.

crs_outline:
Sociophonetics is a dynamic field at the intersection of sociolinguistics and phonetics. This course explores two major domains within sociophonetics: language variation and change and self-presentation and social interaction. We will examine how sociophoneticians address key questions, such as why and how certain linguistic features become widespread and dominant, and how phonetic analysis can illuminate micro-social and sociopsychological mechanisms underpinning linguistic behaviour.

Through a combination of theoretical discussions, hands-on workshops, and critical engagement with research papers, this course provides an in-depth understanding of sociophonetic methodologies and the social factors influencing linguistic variation. The schedule introduces foundational concepts in sociolinguistics (including the first, second, and third waves of sociolinguistics), practical tools (e.g., vowel normalization, principal component analysis), and advanced topics like gender, sexuality, cognitive sociolinguistics, and algorithmic bias. Students will also critically explore broader sociolinguistic theories, such as enregisterment, stylization, and language ideology, with the aim of connecting sociophonetics to larger social and cultural dynamics.

This course is designed for:
	Students interested in sociophonetics and its applications,
	Students aiming to pursue careers in variationist sociolinguistics, and
	Students looking to incorporate social dimensions into their phonetic research but who may be new to sociolinguistic theory.

While we will introduce basic sociolinguistic theories, the primary focus is on applying sociophonetic methodologies to empirical research. Students seeking a deeper theoretical exploration (e.g., language ideology, orders of indexicality) are encouraged to take the "Seminar on Sociolinguistic Theories" after completing this course.

Course Format:
	Taught in English and Mandarin 
	Includes lectures, workshops, and paper discussions.

crs_outline:
The process of filmmaking has always fascinated not only the general audience but also the filmmakers themselves. What happens behind the camera has always made very fascinating stories to be put on screen. In this class, we will watch and discuss the film classics on filmmaking itself made by the film auteurs, who include Buster Keaton, Dziga Vertov, Billy Wilder, Federico Fellini, Jean-Luc Godard, François Truffaut, Robert Altman, Stanley Kwan, the Coen Brothers, Tim Burton, Paul Thomas Anderson, Quentin Tarantino, David Fincher, Tan Chui Mui, as well as Michel Hazanavicius. Together, they, being the most prominent directors in the film history, reveal to us the secret behind the scene and their view on film industry and film as an art form.
Students will be required to watch and discuss a film in class weekly. For the term project (5 pages in length), each student shall choose to write in English either a screenplay or a term paper by the end of the semester. He or she shall decide which track to follow by the midterm that takes the form of a one-on-one interview with the instructor. Other requirements include (1) film logs, (2) online responses, and (3) a presentation on filmmakers. All lectures, assignments, and class discussion will be conducted in English.

crs_outline: Unlike broader ecocriticism, ecofeminism has had to defend itself against accusations of essentialism from wary feminists since its introduction in the 1970s. In effect, ecofeminism has developed with a greater regard for drawing out complicated entanglements between material realities and ideological frameworks. Into the new millennium, inquiries into women-nature relationships have broadened to include diverse approaches such as deep ecology, vegetarianism, planetary health, queer theory, care ethics, new materialism, affect research, and posthuman studies. This course will cover ecofeminism's major commitments and ideologies, with a particular focus on its exploration of and investment in human-animal relationships. Course content includes both critical materials and literary texts.

dep_ename: Department of Foreign Languages and Literatures
crs_outline:
This one-term, weekly course invites undergraduate students to explore the dynamic intersection of history and imagination through the lens of the British historical novel. By engaging in a close reading of canonical works by Sir Walter Scott, Charles Dickens, and Virginia Woolf, students will trace the genre’s evolution from the early nineteenth to the early twentieth century.

The curriculum is designed to introduce students to the essential techniques and analytical skills required for the university-level study of historical fiction. Beyond broadening their understanding of English literature, the course focuses on fostering informed, critical reading and cultivating rigorous scholarly habits.

Key academic components include:
•	Critical Research: Students will conduct literary and historical research, learning to synthesize primary texts with secondary sources.
•	Scholarly Writing: Mastery of professional citation standards, specifically MLA or MHRA formats, is a core requirement for all written assignments.
•	Presentation Skills: Through group oral reports and peer discussion, students will refine their ability to present complex literary arguments effectively.

By the end of the term, students will not only understand how these authors reimagined the past but also how to navigate the boundaries between historical “fact” and narrative “fiction”.

cos_cname: 精神分析與倫理（文類課：其他）
memo: 專選，開放二三四年級學生選修
dep_ename: Department of Foreign Languages and Literatures
crs_outline:
When Sigmund Freud wrote his Totem and Taboo, one of his aims was to vet out the psychological root of Immanuel Kant’s “categorical imperative” that lays the foundation for modern ethics. Since then, however, little advancement has been made in psychoanalysis about the ethical thesis on “how to live.” Second- and third-generation analysts such as Erich Fromm, Melanie Klein, D. W. Winnicott, and Jacques Lacan, though dabbling occasionally in ethical matters, have not made a systematic inquiry into ethics proper either. In this class, we will read mainly two contemporary practicing psychoanalysts whose thoughts on ethics merit a serious attention. Indian-born Salman Akhtar attempts to psychoanalytically define the positive attributes and actions ranging from courage to sacrifice that have helped him to find his footing in racialized America. Christopher Bollas, whose earlier training includes comparative literature, delves into ancient Chinese philosophy to expound on how a modern Chinese speaker would subliminally lead his or her virtuous life. Virtues alone, however, are not enough to make the world a better place unless evils are also fully understood. The penultimate weeks of the class will be devoted to terrorism and fascism in both Lacanian and non-Lacanian perspectives.
	Students will be required to read the weekly assigned materials and write an online response. A term paper of 5 to 7 pages in length in English is required by the end of the semester. Students shall decide on what to write by the midterm that takes the form of a one-on-one interview with the instructor. All reading and writing assignments will be done in English, whereas class discussions might proceed bilingually.

cos_ename: Science Fiction Short Story and Film(Genre: Others)
dep_ename: Department of Foreign Languages and Literatures
crs_outline:
This course explores philosophical questions in science fiction (sf) short fiction, film, and TV series, analyzing them as cultural phenomena reflecting the period in which they were created as well as their importance to us today and the ethical questions they raise. Ethical questions related to the introduction of new technologies and changes in daily life form the focus of investigations. 
Each week we will focus on a theme appearing across multiple works, treating them as variations, whether best described as commercial trends reflecting audience interests, or as simply creative writers and filmmakers engaging looming problems facing societies. Many of the themes engage questions concerning intersections of new technologies and social change, often social justice and human rights as well as ecological issues: what is the role of human autonomy, democracy, and economic orders as a post-scarcity society becomes viable materially but not necessarily politically? 
Various posthuman and dystopian stories offer complex frameworks and heroes facing off in such worlds in which reality itself has been radically shifted.
How might we engage these science-fictional allegories as challenges for us to redefine humanism—human-centered knowledge-production—and invent posthuman critical spaces for mediation between agents and species in ways that would have been unimaginable in the past? 
What points of view, characters, conflicts, and moral frames of engagement are promoted in these works of fiction, film, and streaming TV? What backstories and worlds illustrate and problematize futures that serve as thought experiments, cautionary tales with glimmers of hope?
How are digital and AI-based agents depicted? How can exploring imaginative scenarios, limited by their respective forms of writing and cinematographic storytelling, serve as state propaganda or lobbying for causes, and how does this affect how we appreciate the works? 
What is at stake is reflexively engaged in examining these works, raising philosophical questions from multiple languages and traditions.

課程概述：
本課程授課對象為修畢初級日文的同學。隨課本進度授課，完成全年度學習後，可習得大致為日檢N5程度的日文應用。
課程中將隨各課主題內容講解語彙，並逐項分析各主題句型，透過口說及書寫練習強化同學們對句型的掌握度，也將透過會話演練及課堂活動等，讓同學們進一步活用句型內容，提升日語流暢度及溝通能力。課程中亦將視情況補充日本文化介紹、聽力練習、介紹線上學習資源等，以強化同學的學習興趣，培養主動自發的學習精神。

*授課方式及進度等，仍可能視實際上課情況適當進行調整。


本學期學習重點：
1.L9:  助詞が相關句型（表好惡、理解、擁有等）、敘述因果關係
2. L10: 「存在動詞」應用句型
3. L11: 常用的「數量詞」及應用句型
4. L12: 名詞及形容詞句過去式；形容詞 比較級、最高級句型
5. L13: 願望表現 (敘述想要什麼、想做什麼)、移動目的句型 (去某處做某事)
6. L14: 動詞分類、て形活用變化、て形應用句型 (請託、指示的句型、動作現在進行式等)

學習目標：
1.習得聽、說、讀、寫日語初級語彙及句型的能力
2.能於日常生活中聽、說應用所學句型，具基本日語溝通能力。
3.增進對日本文化的理解
4.提升學生生活品質及未來發展潛力

crs_outline:
不論你是傳播與科技系的學生或是其他科系的傳播科技使用者，都應該對傳播科技的發展有一定的了解。這堂課將幫助同學們了解我們平常使用的傳播科技的發展歷程及其帶來的影響，以及一些與傳播科技相關的重要理論與政策。同時，我們還會針對新興傳播科技，如社群平台、虛擬技術、人工智慧（artificial intelligence, AI）等的發展與可能帶來的影響進行探討。從這堂課程中，同學們將學習到以下面向：

• 重要傳播科技的發展歷程
• 傳播科技在社會中的應用及其重要影響
• 重要傳播科技的政策制訂與影響
• 思考傳播科技對社會、對個人的影響

同學們將在課堂中學到基本傳播科技相關的知識外，更重要的是，學習到批判思考的重要性，並透過不斷練習，培養批判思考與反思能力。

傳科系專業素養選修
costype: 領域課程-個人、社會與文化
crs_outline:
This class addresses the intersection of media audiences, technologies, popular culture, and society by examining the emerging and transforming popular culture of emotions and intimacy. After students are introduced to the key theoretical approaches through media cases and literature from communication and media studies, sociology, critical and feminist theories, and new media studies, we will explore how and to what extent gender and emotions are intrinsically intertwined with media culture and audiences’ practices.
At the end of this class, students are expected to be able to mobilize the theories to study the relationship between media representation, audience practices, and social contexts. In particular, students will understand emotions as a social deployment in the creation of gendered media and consumer culture. Also, by developing critical thinking and analytical skills through the production of a media work or an original research paper, students will become more responsible consumers and producers of popular imagery.

memo:
1. 修課至HK215
2. 模組 A：媒體創作
crs_outline:
隨著AI的興起及3D繪圖技術的進步，虛擬人物、虛擬物件、虛擬場景已成為現今影視製作上不可或缺的要素，影視視覺上的創作不再侷限於現有真實的物體與環境，創新的想像力才是製作上最大的限制。
本課程的目標除學習傳統的現場直播多機作業(EFP)技能外，更透過最先進的Unreal引擎及3D虛擬攝影棚之使用培育對新媒體的創意發想，及創新互動式視覺影像的創作能力。

本課程為本校跨域選修課程，為配合學校對課程的要求，全學期16周的課程將規劃為三個單元:

單元一 基本影棚節目製作:  4周16個小時 (作業一)
本單元為4周16小時之課程，內容以學習運用虛擬攝影棚創作影視節目，課程內容包含，虛擬棚節目設計與規劃、棚內EFP三機作業節目製作及相關影片字幕、配音、剪輯等後製技術教學，因本單元目的在於影棚的基本操作，因此無須用到虛擬場景，以簡單的節目錄製為目標，同學可依個人的專長及興趣選擇相關的職務與工作項目，並共同完成影片。影片製作為團隊分工的創作，此單元作品 佔學期總成績20%。

單元二: 多機現場直播節目(EFP)製作: 6周18個小時 (作業二)
6周18個小時，本單元內容以學習運用現場多機直播作業EFP創作影視節目，課程內容除包含單元一的各項操作與規劃外，需學習多機作業之操作與使用，達到現場直播的應有的基本技能與知識，本單元的作業成績佔學期總成績30%。

單元三: 虛擬數位媒體創作: 6周18個小時，
本單元為同學自行規劃運用Unreal 或虛擬攝影棚創作帶有虛擬場景、物件或人物的虛擬影視節目，同學需學習虛擬場景的運用與虛擬合成軟體的操作與使用，此作品為作業(三)，佔學期總成績40%


本課程所有作業皆為小組作業，因此課堂況缺將列入學期成績佔10%，每個作業皆有小組內評，個小組皆須由小組成員評分小組內每個成員的貢獻度，此貢獻度將作為該作業個人的評分標準。

memo: 模組 A：媒體創作
costype: 領域課程-個人、社會與文化
crs_outline:
當代社會，人們從睜開眼睛就開始不間斷地使用各種媒體。但這個媒體生態(media ecology)卻往往被當權者---國家與資本掌握。國家越發嫻熟的拿著納稅錢進行大外宣或大內宣，運用置入性行銷等手法進行認知作戰，宣傳政績鞏固政權。資本家則建立媒體帝國(media conglomerates)，挾著對文化內容生產的掌控與平台的壟斷，不間斷的傳送廣告和運用大數據與演算法蒐集、儲存與販售使用者的個人資訊。1990年代原本以為網路允諾的烏托邦世界更成現世反諷，黑暗網路與匿名激發的性格惡性，致使網軍、網路小白(Troll)、侵害者肆虐，網路霸凌、出征、甚至出現駭人的如韓國N號房的網路性犯罪事件。隨著網路足跡的陰魂不散，侵害個人的文化權、名譽、甚至逼人至死。 
       然而，文化是聯合國保障的文化公民權(Cultural Citizenship)，牽涉到我們的自我認同、自我表達聲音的權力、多元資訊的接觸權以及針對社會議題進行倡議，推動公共討論與社會變革，維持民主社會的重要根基。
在這堂課，我們介紹傳播領域的一個新興勃發的重要陣地---人民如何運用文化力量，認識自我、獲得培力；對抗國家與資本的宰制，建立另類媒體；針對社會議題，學習如何倡議，表達訴求，引起公共討論與推動變革。

memo: 模組 C：數位設計
crs_outline:
隨著數位科技深入我們的生活，互動式體驗也成為傳播溝通重要的一環。同時，在元宇宙的趨勢下，遊戲引擎的學習也愈發重要。
這門課將嘗試整合理論概念與實作，從不同角度瞭解遊戲等互動式傳播科技對使用者認知、情緒與行為的潛在效果與心理機制，並進一步延伸探討如何將之正向應用於不同領域與主題、打造合適的互動體驗。同時，也將帶領同學認識Unity遊戲引擎以及相關創作工具，並且在定期的課題挑戰中演練熟習工具的使用。課程中將逐步引導同學們根據對相關理論概念與心理機制的理解與掌握，以傳播溝通為目標（例如新聞傳播、廣告行銷、社會議題關懷等），構思並且實際動手創造有趣創新、並能傳達資訊、發揮影響力的互動虛擬體驗。
透過本課程，同學將習得互動虛擬體驗重要理論概念，除能批判性地檢視、思考其潛在效果，也將練習如何活用理論知識解決問題。同時，同學也將經由此課程培養虛擬體驗創作之基礎能力，未來將能應用於不同的領域和情境，落實個人創意、完成互動虛擬體驗作品。

crs_outline:
人類運用知識理解世界，而知識必須奠基於嚴謹的查證、辨析、邏輯推演與富有洞見的詮釋，社會研究方法即在協助我們透過有效的方式，取得有效的資料，對一個研究問題提出有效的解釋，進而在知識上回應對這個世界的關懷。此課程旨在介紹社會研究的邏輯與操作，包括質化與量化研究各自的知識形成觀點與研究分析過程，訓練學生根據自己的關懷與興趣，聚焦凝鍊出好的研究問題，設計有效的研究方法、強化資料蒐集技術，最終藉由豐富的資料，做出精準而有說服力的研究分析。
此課程旨在講授社會研究方法的基礎概念與綜覽，在一學期的時間限制下，將以質化研究為主，量化的部分推薦同學另修社會統計。

crs_outline:
探討人及人的處境是恆常的課題，人文著作也環繞於此主題，人類累積浩瀚的著作，但重點不在於閱讀所有著作，而是從閱讀中產生自己的想法，這也是這門課的核心目的。

依照本系課程架構，經典閱讀分為人文與社會兩組四門課，相對於社會學和人類學，本門課從哲學和心理學兩個領域出發，選擇了多位名家的著作，主要在於探討:當代社會人類的處境、集體潛意識和人類文明、愛的哲學分析、嚮宴、戲劇分析。希望同學對這些主題有興趣，相關的討論也能夠對同學的思想有所幫助。

cos_cname: 博物館的視野：歷史策展、社會對話與 AI 數位實踐
cos_ename: Museum Perspectives: Historical Curation, Social Dialogue, and AI Digital Practice
dep_ename: Department of Humanities and Social Sciences
crs_outline:
本課程旨在打破傳統歷史學科僅限於文本研究的框架，帶領學生走入當代博物館的實務現場。課程結合歷史專業、策展實務、社會對話以及前瞻的數位 AI 工具，培養學生將深厚的人文底蘊轉化為公眾溝通素材的能力。課程內容主要分為五大面向：

1. 博物館與在地脈絡：探討現代博物館的演進，並聚焦「國立故宮博物院」在台灣的特殊歷史脈絡與社會定位，引導學生思考藏品如何與當代社會產生共鳴。

2. 策展規劃與實務：邀請故宮專業研究員，深入解析書畫與器物策展的實務流程，包含展覽企劃撰寫、展件挑選與詮釋、空間動線規劃，以及文物安全考量等策展幕後工作。

3. 社會參與與公眾對話：探討博物館如何透過文創商品設計、親子教育推廣等方式與社會大眾互動。同時邀請研究員分享在「民間文物鑑定」中遭遇的真實故事，探討學術專業與公眾期待間的溝通藝術。

4. 數位人文與 AI：引導學生認識數位浪潮下的博物館轉型，並實務操作當前熱門的 AI 工具。思考如何運用 AI 輔助展場空間模擬、圖像辨識、或多語系導覽稿撰寫，將 AI 視為策展與歷史普及的助力。

5. 實作成果展示：課程強調做中學，期末將安排分組實作。學生需整合所學，利用圖像代替實體文物，並結合數位 AI 工具，策劃舉辦一場微型特展。透過實戰操作與專家講評，具體展現跨域整合與問題解決之能力。

cos_ename: Streaming Media (Netflix, Apple TV+, Disney+)  Film and TV Drama Commentary
dep_ename: Department of Humanities and Social Sciences
crs_outline:
此課程結合文化理論與媒體產業分析，探究網路串流媒體傳播，包括Netflix、Apple TV+、Disney+，已如何轉化全球影視文化。政治與政策也主導數位傳播革命，追溯歷史，了解媒體全球化演變，以及目前不斷發展的全球擴張。電影與電視做為影像廣播媒體媒介，現已經由無線網路傳遞影像至我們的手機螢幕、iPad與電腦。Netflix現是世界上最大最多訂閱觀看用戶的線上點選即播放服務，觀看者想要觀賞的電影與電視影集，滑指之間即可享受，無遠弗界;而且Netflix改變媒體內容的流通。
此課研討在網路世代全球媒體，如何使用串流媒體打破國際地理、商業市場疆界的隔閡，以可行銷全球的影視作品，與國際間的觀眾、市場、機構交流及影響。但也有些問題，舉例: 平台有地區阻隔，(像是「這部片在該地區無法取得撥放」)、播放清單從一國家到另一國家的萎縮與擴張、訂閱價格以不同的貨幣出現、字幕與標題無法提供本土語言等等。此課探究以上種種情況，提供了解數位媒體傳播的真實地理性。Netflix的故事不只包括美國，從阿根廷到澳洲，Netflix由矽谷研發爬升至國際串流線上影視服務，已如何轉換將媒體消費拉至全球(包括歐洲、英國、德國等)跨國規模。
這門課「Netflix媒體影視評析」將可幫助修課學生了解在你我身邊這個複雜不斷變換的串流媒體環境。並且每週搭配教科書課本內容，分析評論數齣精選當代暢銷觀看人數眾多的優質電影與電視影集，例如：階級議題在著名的英國電視影集Downton Abbey (six seasons 2010-2015) , 電影Downton Abbey (2019), 與最新開拍電影Downton Abbey: A New Era (2022)、Bridgerton (1st Season 2020, 2nd Season 2022), 建造法國凡爾賽宮的法王路易十四執政時期政治、外交、領土、戰爭、貴族、平民、性愛、謀殺、神秘鐵面人豐富內容的影集Versailles (2018, 3 Seasons)、美國政治權謀的Netflix自創影集House of Cards (6 seasons, 2013-2018)、揭露現實殘忍競爭的芭蕾舞集Tiny Pretty Things (2020)、 滑冰影集Spinning Out (2020) (研討性、謀殺與奮鬥)，並加入串流媒體Apple TV+之美國女詩人Emily Dickinson (2019)，Disney+之 Star Wars 和 Marvel 兩大 IP 之原創衍生劇：The Mandalorian (2019-2020)與Wandavision (2021)，以及台灣亦於Netflix播放的影集《模仿犯》、《斯卡羅》、《茶金》等，教導學生以戲劇明瞭相關文學、歷史、社會、經濟、政治、感情、人性、戰爭等重要議題。

crs_outline:
本課程以歷史縱深與全球架構的角度，探討從過去到現在人類與農業之間的互動，透過農業反思當代人類生存的選擇策略中的認知運作、文化形塑、政治偏好以及經濟理性，並解析現代社會的病徵與農業變遷所具有的共構關係，而永續未來的決戰點在農業。

因此本課程以不同關懷的理論與實證研究，將食農政治與農糧文化視為一個獨特的方法取徑，從全球鉅觀到在地微觀，檢視環境、資本、國際關係、種族族裔等多重社會面向與農業的交織互動。藉由農業凸顯的自然與社會、農民與其他人、城市與鄉村等等多重張力，本課程最後回到東亞農業的現場，以日本與臺灣為例，檢視地方、區域、全球不同尺度之間的動態與結構性，探問其中萬物的本體存在與價值選擇。

dep_cname: 學士後電子與光子學士學位學程
dep_ename: Electronics and Photonics Post-undergraduate Second Degree Program
crs_outline:
一方面透過實際操作深刻體會課本上虛幻的光學現象與知識，另一方面可習得基本光學實驗技術、儀器原理與光電科技之應用、分析能力，作為未來從事研究的基礎。配合幾項現代應用系統之示範實驗，希望能啟發光學與光電系統實作創造力。
光學實驗室位於基礎科學大樓(科三館,SC360)，實驗室中計有：
幾何光學實驗系統; 光纖技術與特性實驗; 干涉儀實驗系統~邁克遜,牛頓環,法布里-培洛等干涉儀; 光信號處理系統~光的繞射,富氏光學與光信號處理(含光學準晶格); 光偏極化實驗系統; 雷射原理實驗系統; 固態雷射與倍頻實驗系統(含Q開關脈衝雷射與光電量測); 雷射鑷夾; 電光調制實驗(圓錐光干涉); 醫療雷射光電應用系統; 科學攝影技術; Schlieren攝影系統(氣流紋影); SLM空間光相位調製器(LCoS數位光學系統); 色散分光測光源光譜系統~光柵,菱鏡…等相關實驗設備及講義。每學期將從其中組合出6-7大項小組實驗、3-4項大組實驗或示範實驗，每項小組實驗需時一至兩週(視修課人數調整)。

crs_outline:
本課程旨在帶領學生探索微處理機（Microprocessor）的運作原理，並以經典的 8051 單晶片微控制器（Microcontroller）為應用對象。課程內容涵蓋 8051 的內部架構、定址方式、指令集、I/O控制、中斷控制、定時器/計數器以及串列通訊等，透過編寫組合語言（Assembly Language），直接與硬體對話。核心目標在於讓學習者掌握嵌入式系統設計基礎，未來易學習更複雜的微處理機之應用。

This course is designed to guide students in exploring the operational principles of microprocessors, focusing on the application of the classic 8051 microcontroller. It covers the 8051's internal architecture, addressing modes, instruction set, I/O control, interrupt control, timers/counters, and serial communication. By writing assembly language, learners will interact directly with the hardware. The core objective is to enable students to master the fundamentals of embedded system design, laying a solid foundation for learning more complex microprocessor applications in the future.

crs_outline:
本課程為工程領域學生必修之基礎數學課程。內容主要涵蓋單變數微積分之核心理論、多變數微積分基礎（偏微分與多重積分）以及無窮級數。作為一個 3學分的微積分課程，本課程的設計簡化部分邏輯推導與定理證明，著重於工程應用的實務計算能力。特別強調微積分工具與後續專業科目（如電路學、電子學、電磁學、訊號與系統以及工程數學等）的緊密銜接，核心目標是協助學生建立分析現代電子與電磁系統的數學思維。
This course is a required foundational mathematics course for engineering students. The content primarily covers the core theories of single-variable calculus, the fundamentals of multivariable calculus (partial derivatives and multiple integrals), and infinite series. As a three-credit course, it streamlines rigorous logical derivations and theorem proofs to prioritize practical computational skills for engineering applications. Special emphasis is placed on the close connection between calculus tools and subsequent advanced courses (such as Circuit Theory, Electronics, Electromagnetics, Signals and Systems, and Engineering Mathematics), with the core objective of assisting students in developing the mathematical thinking required to analyze modern electronic and electromagnetic systems.

crs_outline:
本課程專為工程領域學生設計，旨在全面性地概述計算機科學 (CS) 的基礎概念和近代運算技術。本課程彌合了硬體和軟體之間的鴻溝，涵蓋資料儲存/處理、算術/邏輯運算、計算機架構、作業系統、演算法和程式語言。此外，學生將被引導探索重要的運算應用，包括嵌入式系統、網路、網際網路、雲端/邊緣運算和資訊安全。本課程也將介紹物聯網 (IoT)、人工智慧 (AI) 和擴增實境 (AR)/虛擬實境 (VR) 等前沿技術趨勢，並以 Python 為實踐工具，培養學生的運算思維和基本程式設計技能。核心目標是透過跨領域 IT 素養的扎根，開拓學生的跨界視野並啟發多元未來。
This course provides a comprehensive overview of fundamental computer science concepts and modern computing technologies tailored for engineering students. It bridges the gap between hardware and software, covering data storage/manipulation, arithmetic/logic operations, computer architecture, operating systems, algorithms, and programming languages. Additionally, students will explore essential computing applications, including embedded systems, networking, the Internet, cloud/edge computing, and information security. The course also introduces cutting-edge technology trends such as IoT, AI, and AR/VR, while utilizing Python as a practical tool to develop algorithmic thinking and basic programming skills. The core objective is to equip students with a solid, cross-disciplinary IT foundation, broaden students' horizons and inspire diverse futures.

crs_outline:
一方面透過實際操作深刻體會課本上虛幻的光學現象與知識，另一方面可習得基本光學實驗技術、儀器原理與光電科技之應用、分析能力，作為未來從事研究的基礎。配合幾項現代應用系統之示範實驗，希望能啟發光學與光電系統實作創造力。
光學教學實驗室位於育成大樓KC107，實驗室中計有：
幾何光學實驗系統; 光纖技術與特性實驗; 干涉儀實驗系統~邁克遜,牛頓環,法布里-培洛等干涉儀; 光信號處理系統~光的繞射,富氏光學與光信號處理; 光偏極化實驗系統; 雷射原理、固態雷射與倍頻實驗系統; 電光調制實驗; 醫療雷射光電應用系統; 科學攝影; SLM空間光相位調製器(LCoS數位光學系統); 光譜…等相關實驗設備及講義。

properties of wave function are also discussed. The topics we discuss are:

(3) Semiclassical approximation
(3) Bra-Ket notation
(4) Schrodinger equation in 3D space
(5) The hydrogen atom 
(6) Angular momentum and spin

memo: [English Medium Course]
crs_outline:
This course introduces fundamental concepts applicable to biomedical instrumentation systems. Topics include the static and dynamic characteristics of measurement systems, the engineering design process, commercial development pathways, regulatory classifications, and electrical safety standards for medical devices. 
The course emphasizes practical design principles, enabling students with limited electronics backgrounds to develop instruments that may not be commercially available. Students will learn the principles underlying various sensor mechanisms, analog signal processing (including amplifier and filter design), and digital data acquisition, processing, storage, and display using microcontrollers. 
Applications covered include cardiovascular and respiratory measurements, biosensors, clinical laboratory instrumentation, medical imaging systems, as well as selected therapeutic and prosthetic devices. 
Course Goals:
1.	Emphasize engineering design principles to enable students to develop medical instrumentation systems.
2.	Provide updated coverage of modern sensor technologies and signal processing techniques.
3.	Introduce contemporary microcontroller applications in biomedical instrumentation.
4.	Present revised and updated chapters, descriptions, and references reflecting current advancements.
5.	Strengthen analytical and problem-solving skills through comprehensive worked examples.
6.	Provide supplementary learning materials via a companion webpage.
7.	Offer a solutions manual containing complete solutions to all problems for instructional support.
