memo: [English Medium Course]
dep_cname: 醫學生物技術暨檢驗學系
dep_ename: Department of Biotechnology and Laboratory Science in Medicine
crs_outline:
課程概述
本課程系統性介紹分子生物技術的基本原理、實作方法及其在醫藥、診斷、治療與生技產業中的應用。課程內容涵蓋重組DNA技術、蛋白質與核酸治療、分子診斷、基因與細胞治療、疫苗開發、轉殖動植物技術等，並探討其實際應用與未來發展。透過講授與期中考評量，學生將能掌握關鍵技術並建立跨領域整合能力。

課程目標
1. 瞭解重組DNA與分子複製技術的基本操作與應用場域。
2. 掌握原核與真核系統中重組蛋白的生產流程與規模放大策略。
3. 認識分子診斷、蛋白質與核酸治療、免疫療法、疫苗設計的最新進展。
4. 探討基因與細胞治療、轉殖動植物等技術於臨床與產業之潛力。
5. 建立基因體與蛋白質體整合分析的能力，理解生物資訊於現代生技的角色。
6. 培養學生跨領域整合與科技應用的能力，理解分子技術如何解決實際問題。

Course Description
This course provides a comprehensive overview of molecular biotechnology, covering the fundamental principles and techniques of recombinant DNA technology, molecular cloning, and their applications in medicine, diagnostics, therapeutics, and the biotech industry. Topics include recombinant protein production, nucleic acid therapeutics, molecular diagnostics, gene and cell therapy, vaccines, and transgenic organisms. Students will gain both theoretical understanding and practical insight through structured lectures and examinations.

Course Objectives
1. Understand the fundamentals of recombinant DNA and molecular cloning technologies.
2. Learn the production and scale-up processes for recombinant proteins in prokaryotic and eukaryotic systems.
3. Explore current advancements in molecular diagnostics, protein and nucleic acid therapeutics, immunotherapy, and vaccine development.
4. Analyze the principles and applications of gene therapy, cell therapy, and transgenic organisms.
5. Develop competency in integrating genomics, proteomics, and bioinformatics in biotechnology.
6. Foster interdisciplinary thinking and apply molecular biotechnology to solve real-world biomedical problems.

crs_outline:
開設宗旨: 這是一堂為提昇整體治療醫學品質﹑精進醫學學術研究水準所開的課程。  授課目的在介紹問卷調查研究設計和分析﹑和執行此類研究的方法﹑包括講授各類研究設計﹑各種工具﹑分析方法﹑及推論。課程內容:  介紹問卷調查研究設計﹑和執行此類研究的方法， 包括講授各類研究種類﹑各種工具﹑研究問題設計、落實及量化理論假說與研究目標、選樣、信效度評估、變數設定、統計及分析方法﹑推論。 並介紹心理認知方法以偵測敏感或隱瞞的真實答案，及如何撰寫研究報告。本課程之重要性: 此類研究實際調查的資料,將有助於提供未來治療病患多方位的醫療所需指標, 或協助制定與修正健保醫療政策。因此﹑實有必要開設專門課程﹑以培養學生思考和評估問題﹑設計和執行此類研究的能力。

crs_outline: 本課程以聚合酶連鎖反應（PCR）及核酸應用技術為主軸，系統性介紹核酸檢測、分子診斷與新興核酸工程技術的理論基礎與實務應用。課程內容由 PCR 基本原理出發，逐步延伸至 PCR-based detection methods、aptamer 在診斷與治療中的應用、DNA circuit reaction、DNA microarray 之製備與分析，以及等溫核酸擴增檢測技術等主題。透過本課程，學生將理解不同核酸檢測平台的設計邏輯、反應機制與應用情境，並能掌握其在疾病診斷、生物標誌物偵測、精準醫療與生醫研究中的角色。課程亦納入 DNA origami 等進階核酸奈米技術，帶領學生認識核酸分子作為可程式化材料在生物醫學與奈米科技領域的發展潛力。整體課程設計兼具基礎理論與前沿應用，旨在培養學生對 PCR 與核酸相關技術的整合性理解，強化其分析分子檢測策略、評估技術適用性，以及銜接後續研究與實驗設計的能力。課程採隔週授課方式進行，並於期末進行報告式評量。

dep_ename: Department of Biotechnology and Laboratory Science in Medicine
crs_outline:
課程綱要(中)
幹細胞生物學、生物技術與應用科學的進展持續推動醫學研究與創新療法的發展，而尖端的生物資訊平台與開放資料庫則加速了精準醫學與標靶治療的進步。本課程將介紹癌症治療相關的重要概念與方法學，並結合實作訓練，讓學生能夠實際操作文獻中常見的工具。透過這樣的學習過程，學習者將同時獲得理論知識與應用技能，不僅能夠批判性地解讀研究成果，設計有效的癌症檢測與治療流程，亦能培養獨立學習的能力。

教學目標(中)	
透過本課程，學生將能建立對幹細胞生物學、癌症生物學與生物資訊學之核心概念的紮實理解，並學習這些領域如何交互作用以推動醫學研究與治療創新。他們將具備運用尖端生物資訊平台與開放資料庫的能力，以支持標靶治療與精準醫學的發展。透過實作訓練，學生將強化技術技能，熟悉文獻中廣泛使用的工具，並培養獨立學習的能力。最終，學習者將能批判性地解讀研究成果，設計有效的癌症檢測與治療流程，並將理論知識轉化為生物醫學與製藥領域中的實際應用。預期學習成效如下:
1. 描述並理解幹細胞生物學、癌症生物學與生物資訊學中的關鍵術語與概念。
2. 比較各種癌症診斷方法，並闡述生物醫學與製藥產業中最前沿的癌症治療策略。
3. 應用開放資源與整合資料庫，在特定情境下預測癌症患者的臨床結果。
4. 設計一個全面且個人化的流程，用於癌症的檢測、治療與後續追蹤照護。

課程綱要(英) 
Advances in stem cell biology, biotechnology, and applied science continue to drive medical research and the development of innovative therapeutics, while cutting-edge bioinformatics platforms and open-source databases accelerate progress in targeted therapy and precision medicine. This course introduces essential concepts and methodologies for developing cancer treatments and integrates hands-on training to provide students with practical experience using tools commonly employed in the literature. Through this approach, learners will gain both theoretical understanding and applied skills, enabling them to critically interpret research, design effective workflows for cancer detection and treatment, and cultivate the capacity for independent learning.

教學目標(英) 
Through this course, students will develop a solid understanding of the fundamental concepts in stem cell biology, cancer biology, and bioinformatics, and learn how these fields intersect to advance medical research and therapeutic innovation. They will acquire the ability to navigate and apply cutting-edge bioinformatics platforms and open-source databases to support targeted therapy and precision medicine. By engaging in hands-on practice, students will strengthen their technical skills, gain experience with tools widely used in the literature, and cultivate the capacity for independent learning. Ultimately, learners will be equipped to critically interpret research findings, design effective workflows for cancer detection and treatment, and translate theoretical knowledge into practical applications in biomedical and pharmaceutical contexts. The intended learning outcomes are summarized below.
(1). To describe and understand key terminology and concepts in stem cell biology, cancer biology, and bioinformatics.
(2). To compare various approaches to cancer diagnosis and highlight cutting-edge cancer therapeutics in the biomedical and pharmaceutical industries.
(3). To apply open-source materials and integrated databases to predict clinical outcomes of cancer patients under defined scenarios.
(4). To design a comprehensive, personalized pipeline for cancer detection, treatment, and follow-up care.

課程概述：
癌症細胞生物學是一門研究所課程，旨在讓學生深入了解癌症發生、進展和轉移的細胞和分子機制。本課程著重於探討癌症特徵以及相應的治療和預防策略。透過課堂講解、生物資訊學工具的實踐、問題導向學習 (PBL) 演示和科學寫作作業的結合，學生將全面理解癌症細胞生物學，為他們未來在腫瘤學的進階研究或臨床實踐做好準備。
課程目標：
在本課程結束時，學生將能夠：
1. 敘述癌細胞生物學的基本概念與關鍵過程
2. 認識癌症的生物學特徵
3. 探索癌症療法和疫苗的開發
4. 在癌症研究中應用生物資訊學工具和生物醫學技術
5. 培養科學的口語、寫作和批判性思考能力
Course Overview:
Cancer Cell Biology is a graduate-level course designed to provide students with an in-depth understanding of the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying cancer development, progression, and metastasis. This course will emphasize the exploration of the cancer hallmarks and the corresponding treatment and prevention strategies. Through a combination of lectures, hands-on practice with bioinformatics tools, problem-based learning (PBL) presentations, and writing assignments, students will gain comprehensive knowledge and practical skills essential for advanced research and clinical practice in oncology.
Course Objectives:
By the end of this course, students will be able to:
1.	Introduce the fundamental concepts and key processes in cancer cell biology
2.	Recognize the biological hallmarks of cancer
3.	Explore the development of cancer therapy and vaccines
4.	Apply bioinformatics tools and biomedical techniques in cancer research
5.	Develop scientific speaking, writing, and critical thinking skills

memo: 本課程與分子生物學合班上課
dep_cname: 生化暨分子生物研究所
dep_ename: Institute of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
crs_outline:
"本研究所課程分為三大部份，修習前兩部份為三學分，三部份全修習為四學分。課程的第一部分著重於蛋白質的結構和分類，核酸的結構、染色體和基因組的組織，以及DNA的複製、重組和修復過程。同時，學生們也會學習蛋白質的功能，包括其參與的生化反應和分子交互作用。課程的第二部分將探討核膜和染色體組織的相關課題。學生們將瞭解核膜的結構和功能，以及染色體組織和結構的原理和機制。此外，學生們也將學習轉錄過程中的關鍵概念，包括基因的轉錄和轉錄調控，以及表觀遺傳學的原理和影響。課程的第三部分將涵蓋RNA的調控和非編碼RNA生物學的重要性。學生們將研究轉譯過程中的關鍵概念，並探討轉譯的調控機制。此外，學生們還將學習生物能量學和氧化代謝，以及碳水化合物、胺基酸、脂質和核苷酸代謝的調控機制。

這門課程旨在培養學生對生物分子和其功能的深入理解，以及生化反應的調控機制。通過學習這些核心主題，學生們將能夠進一步探索生物化學和分子生物學領域的研究和應用潛力。"

crs_outline:
"本課程「核磁共振在生物學之應用」，旨在結合基礎理論與核心實務操作，帶領學生全面掌握生物分子核磁共振技術。課程內容涵蓋 Linux 基本操作、NMR 基本原理、儀器構造，並著重於大量的實作訓練，包含儀器調諧與鎖場（tuning/shimming/locking）、1D/2D/3D 實驗設定，以及操作 NMRPipe 與 Sparky 等專業軟體進行數據處理與化學位移指認，全面培養學生在生化研究領域中的關鍵實驗與分析技能。

英文課程說明 (English Version)
The ""Practical Aspects of Biomolecular NMR,"" is designed to provide students with a comprehensive, hands-on understanding of NMR spectroscopy in biological applications. The curriculum effectively bridges foundational theory with extensive practical training, covering essential topics such as basic Linux operation, NMR principles, and instrumentation. Students will gain direct experience in instrument tuning, running 1D/2D/3D experiments, and using specialized software like NMRPipe and Sparky for data processing and chemical shift assignment, equipping them with critical skills for advanced biomolecular research."

crs_outline: 這門課程是一個廣泛的研究生物技術和生物分子相關領域的介紹。這門課程首先涵蓋了重組DNA技術，學生將了解到基因工程的基本原理和技術，包括DNA重組、載體構築和基因轉染等。接著，課程深入探討了蛋白質結構生物學，學生將學習到蛋白質的結構和功能之間的關係，以及蛋白質的三維結構解析方法，包含核磁共振（NMR）技術。學生也將學習到蛋白質間相互作用的機制，包括蛋白質結合和信號傳遞等重要概念。此外，課程還涵蓋了基因編輯技術，以及這些技術在基因治療和基因功能研究中的應用。學生將學習到蛋白質體學的方法和技術，與基因和蛋白質傳遞的方法和應用。課程還介紹了RNA相關的研究技術，包括RNA合成、修飾和分析等。學生也將學習到RNA干擾的原理和應用，以及基因表達的調控機制。此外，學生將學習到定量聚合酶鏈反應（Q-PCR）和微陣列分析技術，以及這些技術在基因表達研究中的應用。課程涵蓋了螢光蛋白在細胞生物學中的應用，並探討了不同類型的顯微鏡技術。最後，學生還將瞭解轉基因和基因定位在小鼠中的應用，以及相關的技術和方法。

crs_outline:
1. 目標：
此課程是針對碩士班學生安排的統整課程, 除專業知識講授外, 亦包含生命科學領域新穎技術的介紹, 協助學生銜接基礎與進階知識, 並應用於生命科學領域的研究上。
This course is an integrated course designed for graduate students. It introduces not only basic knowledge but also new techniques in life sciences. It expects to help students link basic and advanced knowledge and apply it to research.
2. 課程概述：
藉由整合生命科學相關的生物化學、分子生物學、細胞學、遺傳學、生理學等基礎知識，以細胞的角度、分子的層次更深入探討下列主題： (1)細胞內基因與基因體的結構及演化; (2)核酸與蛋白質的結構、合成的機制、功能及應用; (3)細胞內能量的生成與代謝反應恆定。
This course introduces life phenomena and the function of the cell at the molecular level. The course integrates general knowledge of Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Genetics, and Physiology to explore Life phenomena at molecular and cellular levels and bring advanced knowledge of life sciences to graduate students.
The textbook listed below will be used as the primary material for this subject and which contains the following topics:
1.	Cells, DNA and chromosomes 
2.	Genomes and Genome evolution
3.	Proteins, structure and enzymes
4.	DNA replication, repair and recombination
5.	RNA transcription and protein translation
6.	Control of gene expression
7.	Cell metabolism and cellular homeostatsis

cos_ename: Principles and practice of magnetic resonance image of the human brain (1)
crs_outline:
本課程將讓修課學生系統性的了解功能性及結構性磁振造影分析之相關基礎分析原理,並搭配上機操作及相關文獻導讀之方式增進學生動手實作之能力以協助其未來自身之研究發展. 
本課程有以下三大目標: 
1.建立學生對於功能性磁振造影、高解析度結構性磁振造影以及磁振頻譜影像之基本分析概念. 
2.利用影像學分析軟體之實際操作以了解理論基礎之實際應用情形並增進相關實作能力. 
3.藉由文獻選讀及上台報告方式增進學生科學演講報告能力.

本課程旨在深入探討病毒的分子生物學特性、感染機制與與宿主之交互作用，涵蓋動物病毒的複製策略、基因調控、病毒顆粒組裝與釋放、慢性感染與潛伏感染，以及病毒引發的疾病機轉。課程亦將介紹病毒載體應用、以及當代病毒學前沿議題。
課程目標在於培養學生具備分析與整合病毒學研究文獻的能力，理解病毒在分子與細胞層級的作用機制，並能應用相關知識於病毒學研究、臨床應用或公共衛生領域。

dep_cname: 微生物及免疫學研究所
crs_outline:
課程概述：
1. 本學期我們將討論6個EBV議題，詳見授課內容及參考文獻。
2. 負責老師將選定每週討論議題，並規定1篇課前需閱讀的文獻。
3. 總共有6個討論的議題，每個議題有兩堂課。
a. 第一堂課的第一個小時，由主責學生介紹文章；第二小時由小組討論文章重點及相互解疑，並提出問題供第二次的課程討論，並由負責同學彙整後將文字檔上傳，供同學及老師下載。
b. 第二堂課由主責同學帶領，共同討論同學及老師在第一堂課提出的問題及衍申議題；每組由一位學生負責解釋該組的提問及衍申議題。

memo: [English Medium Course]環工所學生優先。
cos_ename: Management of Contaminated Land and Groundwater
crs_outline:
Contamination of land and groundwater is an increasingly serious problem facing environmental and geoenvironmental professionals nowadays. The adverse and harmful impacts of soil and groundwater contamination are long lasting and the environmental damage may even be irreversible. Therefore, proper management of contaminated land and groundwater is vital for the protection of public health and sustainable development of mankind. However, management of contaminated land and groundwater is a complex and multi-disciplinary subject spanning across politics, public administration, socio-economics, sciences etc.
The primary objective of the course is to provide graduate students with exposure to the different facets of contamination management, from prevention to remediation. At the end of the course, the students who fulfill the requirements of this course should be able to understand the importance, considerations, objectives and strategies of contamination management, to delineate subsurface contamination, to quantify the transport and fate of contaminants in the subsurface, to understand available technologies for remediation of contaminated soil and groundwater, and to develop plans for proper management and/or remediation of contaminated land and groundwater.
Each student is required to select a relevant topic of his/her choice to perform independent research and to present his/her findings in a term paper written in English following the format of a scientific journal of his/her choice. The best papers may be invited to present at seminars of the Institute of Environmental Engineering. The term paper will be due at the final examination.

crs_outline:
本課程聚焦動態系統的建模、模擬、估測與最佳化，涵蓋以下核心內容：
1. 建模方法：基於物理機理與數據融合驅動的動態系統建模方法，包含時域/頻域參數化建模、機器學習與深度神經網路建模，以及其對應的數學函式解析與理論推導。
2. 系統分析：著重時間演化系統之數學描述、機電工程系統之控制器設計，以及模型模擬與驗證流程，確保系統行為之準確性與可靠性。
3. 智能演算法：導入機器學習之分類與迴歸演算法，並延伸至模型強化學習之應用，以提升系統決策與適應能力。
本課程透過數學建模與計算模擬技術，培養動態系統分析與優化之核心能力，強調理論推導與實務應用的整合。學生將掌握從物理現象至數學模型，再到電腦模擬的完整方法論，並學習機器學習於動態系統建模與模擬的進階應用技術。
課程大綱:
(1) 時域/頻域/神經網路系統建模之基礎學理
(2) 工程或物理現象與系統模型數學函式的模擬
(3) 機器學習(Machine Learning)動態建模、模擬與分類
(4) 強化學習(Reinforcement Learning)建模、模擬與控制

The focus of this course is on modeling, simulation, estimation, and optimization of dynamic systems. Concepts taught in this course include physics-based and empirical modeling, dynamic modeling, machine learning and model-free reinforcement learning. For this purpose, the methods to mathematically describe time-evolving systems, the method of system modeling and design of controller for mechanical and electrical engineering systems, machine learning classification and regression are applied.

課程目標:

	使學生具備分析工程問題的能力，運用工程知識和工程模擬程序解決問題。
	學生將能夠收集和分析時間序列數據，以構建數據驅動的系統控制策略。
	學生將能夠制定和執行一個項目，該項目利用機器學習中的課程主題和針對新應用程序的優化方法。
	To train students in the theory and application of modeling dynamical systems using physics and machine learning.
	Students will be able to use different modeling methods to give appropriate dynamic description to the system.
	Enable students to have the ability to analyze engineering problems, and use engineering knowledge and engineering analysis simulation programs to solve problems.
	Students will be able to collect and analyze time-series data to construct data-driven system control strategies.
	Students will be able to formulate and execute a project that utilizes course topics and optimization methods for new applications in machine learning.

The goal of this course is to provide an understanding of numerical methods applied to engineering problems in hydrology and hydraulics. •       Explicit and implicit finite difference methods.
•       Analysis of convergence, stability, and accuracy of numerical schemes.

crs_outline:
Lattice gauge theory (LGT) represents one of the most powerful and advanced formalisms in science to study the most fundamental dynamics of atomic and sub-atomic systems. It has applications that range from condensed matter to particle theory, from the study of phase transitions to quantum scattering.

In this course we will learn the formalism to address the physics of systems that interact via the exchange of gauge bosons. These are called Yang-Mills theories and we will discuss them both with Abelian and non-Abelian gauge groups. Expanding our findings to theories that also include scalar particles we will study the physics of the Higgs boson in the Standard Model. By pushing even further and adding in fermions we will finally arrive at a fully non-perturbative description of quantum chromodynamics, the theory of the strong force. 

Our research will lead us to the realisation that a full result requires the numerical simulation of the system on a (super-)computer and we will practice how to perform such simulations. In addition we will learn how to derive meaningful physics results that cannot be obtained any other way. Throughout emphasis is put on practical implementations.

This course is the first part of a two-part series. Wanting to perform numerical calculations access to a laptop with internet connection is required as well as some interest in writing Python programs. During the course we will develop codes for:
- The bootstrap resampling and fitting of data with a linear ansatz
- The simulation of the Ising Model using a Heatbath algorithm
- The simulation of scalar field theory using the Hybrid Monte Carlo algorithm
- Inversion of a fermion matrix using the Conjugate Gradient algorithm

cos_ename: Trustworthy AI: Statistical Machine Learning and Optimization
crs_outline:
This course centers on Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence (TAI) and integrates methods from statistical machine learning and optimization to examine challenges faced by AI systems in real-world applications, including interpretability, uncertainty, reliability, and decision quality. The course guides students to understand, from the perspectives of data, models, decision-making, and deployment, that AI models should not only pursue predictive accuracy but also be understandable, verifiable, correctable, and capable of supporting robust decisions in complex and changing environments.

Topics include foundational concepts of trustworthy AI, explainable AI, uncertainty quantification, and data-driven decision-making and optimization. Through homework assignments, paper reading, oral presentations, and a final project, students will learn to analyze limitations of AI systems, select and design appropriate statistical machine learning and optimization methods, and translate analyses into practically meaningful or research-relevant models, evidence, and decision recommendations.

After completing this course, students will be able to:
- Understand core concepts of trustworthy AI, statistical machine learning, and optimization, and apply them appropriately to data analysis, model evaluation, and decision-support problems.
- Analyze trustworthy AI issues such as interpretability, uncertainty, and reliability, and evaluate their impacts on model usage and decision quality.
- Develop the ability to read academic papers, structure problems, and communicate research ideas clearly on trustworthy-AI-related topics.
- Integrate statistical machine learning, optimization, and application contexts to design new analytical methods or validation procedures, and present effectiveness and limitations in a project format.

Course learning goals include:
- Critical thinking: Understand the systemic nature of trustworthy AI problems, application contexts, and sources of risk.
- Research skills: Learn how to search for, read, organize, and critique trustworthy AI literature.
- Integrative skills: Design new methods and validation pipelines, and clearly explain advantages, limitations, and applicable scenarios.

Course Scope:
This course does not aim to comprehensively cover all modern AI topics, such as LLMs, computer vision, VLMs, reinforcement learning, or agentic AI. Instead, it mainly approaches trustworthy AI from the perspectives of statistical machine learning, uncertainty quantification, explainability, reliability, and optimization-based decision-making. However, final project topics are open-ended and may involve any AI-related application, as long as they address trustworthy AI issues.

本課程以可信任人工智慧為核心，結合統計機器學習與最佳化方法，探討人工智慧系統在真實應用場域中所面臨的可解釋性、不確定性、可靠性、與決策品質等議題。課程引導學生從資料、模型、決策與系統部署的角度，理解 AI 模型不只是追求預測準確率，也必須能被理解、被檢驗、被修正，並在複雜且變動的環境中支援穩健決策。

課程內容涵蓋可信任 AI 的基本概念、可解釋人工智慧、不確定性量化、資料驅動決策與最佳化等主題。學生將透過作業、論文閱讀、口頭報告與專題實作，學習如何分析 AI 系統的限制，選擇與設計合適的統計機器學習與最佳化方法，並將分析結果轉化為具實務意義或研究價值的模型、證據與決策建議。

修習本課程後，學生將能夠：
- 掌握可信任 AI、統計機器學習與最佳化的基本概念，並能正確應用於資料分析、模型評估與決策支援問題。
- 理解可解釋性、不確定性、分佈變動與模型更新等可信任 AI 議題，並能評估其對模型使用與決策品質的影響。
- 培養學術論文閱讀、問題整理與研究表達能力，能針對可信任 AI 相關主題提出清楚的研究觀點。
- 整合統計機器學習、最佳化與應用情境，設計新的分析方法或驗證流程，並以專題形式呈現其有效性與限制。

本課程的學習目標，包含：
- 思辨能力：理解可信任 AI 問題的系統性、應用脈絡與風險來源。
- 研究能力：學習如何搜尋、閱讀、整理與評論可信任 AI 相關論文。
- 整合型能力：設計新方法、建立驗證流程，並能清楚說明方法的優點、限制與適用情境。

課程範圍：
本課程並非旨在完整涵蓋所有現代人工智慧主題，例如大型語言模型、電腦視覺、視覺語言模型、強化學習或 Agentic AI。相較之下，本課程主要從統計機器學習、不確定性量化、可解釋性、可靠性，以及以最佳化為基礎的決策制定等角度切入可信任人工智慧。期末專題主題採開放形式，可涵蓋任何 AI 相關應用；但專題內容需回應可信任人工智慧相關議題。

crs_outline:
Spectroscopy and microscopy have become essential research tools in modern physical chemistry and a wide range of interdisciplinary research fields, including biomedical science, materials science, and nanotechnology. The objective of this course is to introduce the fundamental principles and research applications of spectroscopic and microscopic techniques commonly used in physical chemistry and related research areas.
The course will begin with the basic concepts of optics and light–matter interactions, followed by introductions to optical components, light sources, detectors, and instrumental systems. Building upon these foundations, the course will cover the operating principles and applications of major spectroscopic and microscopic techniques, including absorption spectroscopy, fluorescence spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, nonlinear spectroscopy, fluorescence microscopy, confocal microscopy, and multiphoton microscopy. The course will also incorporate examples from real research systems and experimental setups to illustrate how these techniques are integrated and applied in modern research laboratories.
Through this course, students will develop a fundamental understanding of spectroscopic and microscopic research techniques, gain familiarity with commonly used experimental instruments and methodologies, and enhance their ability to understand and apply modern research tools in physical chemistry and interdisciplinary sciences.

crs_outline:
Laser Chemistry is a graduate-level course that provides an advanced introduction to the principles and applications of lasers in chemistry. The course focuses on the interaction between light and matter, laser spectroscopy, photochemical and photophysical processes, and laser-based methods for probing and controlling molecular and material systems.

The course will cover both fundamental concepts and selected advanced topics, including molecular spectroscopy, reaction dynamics, nonlinear optical processes, laser-induced heating, optical trapping, laser-induced crystallization, and laser-based manipulation of soft matter and molecular assemblies. Through lectures, discussions, and examples from recent research, students will learn how laser techniques are applied to investigate chemical structures, molecular dynamics, reaction mechanisms, and materials processes.

Course Objectives:
By the end of this course, students will be able to:

Explain the fundamental principles of lasers and laser–matter interactions.
Understand the theoretical basis and practical applications of laser spectroscopy.
Describe photochemical and photophysical processes induced by laser irradiation.
Discuss how lasers can be used to probe, control, and manipulate molecular and material systems.
Critically evaluate recent research examples involving laser chemistry, laser trapping, laser-induced crystallization, and related phenomena.
Apply concepts of laser chemistry to their own research fields in chemistry, materials science, photochemistry, and related areas.

crs_outline:
Introduction to Electrodynamics (ED).
Few theories have been as formative for the development of modern science as classical electrodynamics. Formulated in the late 1800’s and refined in the early 1900’s to this day it forms the solid basis of most day-to-day physics phenomena we observe and use in our technologies. In this course we will study ED from its inception in Maxwell’s equations and develop it towards its covariant formulation. Along the way we will encounter and solve problems in Electro-/Magnetostatics, Radiation Theory, ED in Matter, Electromagnetic Waves and the Lagrangian formulation of classical field theories.

crs_outline:
Course Descriptions and Objectives:

In order to cope with the dynamic environment of global business and industry, this course provides the students with the practical applications of the Intellectual Property (IP) Management and essential business laws across national borders. The content of the course includes Contract Law, IP Laws and Enforcement, IP Contracts and Licensing, US Import/Export Control Management, Business Applications of Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence, Corporate Governance and Boards of Directors, Corporate Merger and Acquisitions, International Commercial Arbitration, Law of World Trade and International Investment Law.

The course starts from providing the overview of the topics of each session and then will provide basic introduction about legal concepts, and legal systems for the students who are not familiar with the study of law. Contract Law will be introduced first as it is fundamental to obtaining a basic understanding of the concept of law. The course goes on to focus on Legal Aspect of IP: Patent Practice, Infringement Analysis and Design Around, IP Litigations and Licensing are the core subjects. 
Subjects such as corporate law, international sales of goods, international commercial arbitration and international investment law are also essential for a corporation engaging in practices across national borders. The other half of this course thus involves these critical national and international laws on business. In addition to the IP-related aspects of the international business laws, this course will provide students with an overview and in-depth introduction on the international business laws essential to business strategy. The major themes cover the aspects of the daily operations as well as the long-term developments of the enterprises, including the following topics:

(1)	Corporate Law: Corporate Governance, U.S. and Transnational Merger and Acquisition, and legal aspects of starting a new business will be introduced.
(2)	Intellectual Property Law: International IP Law, Patent Law, Trade Secret Law.
(3)	Technology and Law: Deep Learning, Blockchain, Artificial Intelligence and Digital Trade.  
(4)	Laws on Biotechnology and Medicine: Medical tourism, disputes and litigation in Taiwan; Pharmaceutical patents and corporate social responsibility.

crs_outline: Stochastic thermodynamics extends classical thermodynamics to individual fluctuating trajectories of small systems, such as colloidal particles, molecular motors, proteins, cells, quantum dots, single-electron transistors, and cold atoms. While classical thermodynamics focuses on average quantities like energy, heat, work, and entropy, stochastic thermodynamics accounts for strong thermal fluctuations at microscopic scales, treating quantities such as heat and work as random variables that vary from one trajectory to another. Information thermodynamics further extends this framework by explicitly incorporating information as a physical quantity that can be quantified, manipulated, and converted into energetic costs or gains. The goal of this course is to equip students with the skills needed to analyze and solve problems involving such small systems across these diverse physical settings.

crs_outline: 在競爭特別激烈的現代商業環境中，公司未來的競爭力取決公司是否能善用其資金，特別是高科技產業，因此資本投資對公司的未來有著絕對的影響。資本投資一經決定，公司未來相關的產品的成本也一同被決定，連同公司未來的競爭力也會受影響。因此，許多公司用資本投資作為策略性或戰略性的工具以獲得市場上有利地位。資本投資計劃的評估更顯得其在企業管理的重要性，而且更應是管理重要的一環。本課程著重在教導學生，於實務面如何評估資本投資案、其評估的方法、及各相關主題。

crs_outline: 本課程聚焦產業暨科技發展的國際布局與策略部署趨勢分析。當穩定的全球安全體系不再、當穩定的全球金融體系逐漸崩壞、當世界貿易組織的遊戲規則遭到侵蝕、當科技研發成果未能平衡經濟發展果實、當全球關鍵資源被利益團體集中掌控、當地緣戰爭不斷爆發、當世界和平一再受到威脅、當病毒疫情繁衍持續嚴峻、當我們期望憧憬的美麗新世界看似即將成為泡影，當不可預期的黑天鵝、灰犀牛突然出現，但當我們仍然擁抱著夢想，當這些政治經濟因素衝擊我們產業暨科技發展與轉型的當下，促進新競合策略的思考：運用制度與政策創新、結合產業創新以相輔相成。面對相關問題逐一釐清本源與衝擊，帶領研究所同學們思考並尋找出解決之道。

crs_outline:
We live inside systems: hospitals, semiconductor supply chains, drone delivery networks, traffic infrastructure, and many others. None of these are built by one expert or one discipline. They are built by teams who must agree on what the system should do, who it serves, what situations it must handle, and how every part connects, behaves, and is verified. That disciplined agreement — structured, traceable, and tested against reality — is what systems engineering exists to produce.
This course begins with a simple question: what is a system? A system is not only a collection of parts. It is defined by boundaries, relationships, interfaces, behaviors, constraints, and emergent outcomes. Learning to see these connections is the foundation of systems thinking. We will study systems engineering as both a technical discipline and a leadership discipline. Systems engineers help teams clarify stakeholder needs, define Use Cases, resolve conflicts, evaluate trade-offs, control changes, and turn complex intentions into buildable and verifiable designs.
In the AI era, this discipline becomes even more important. Large language models and agentic AI tools can accelerate development, but they also require stronger judgment, traceability, verification, and human ownership. Specifications may evolve faster, but change still must be controlled. Systems may become more adaptive, but safety and accountability cannot be lost.  In this course, you will first learn traditional document-based systems engineering: CONOPS, Use Cases, requirements, functional architecture, interfaces, verification plans, and traceability matrices. You will then move into Model-Based Systems Engineering, or MBSE, where interconnected models make system structure, behavior, requirements, Use Cases, interfaces, and verification logic more visible and consistent.
Students will also use AI-assisted tools to support modeling and documentation, while learning to audit, question, and own what those tools produce. By the end of this semester, you will not only know about systems engineering. You will have practiced it — from stakeholder needs and Use Cases to a connected, traceable, and verifiable system design. The goal is to help students think like a systems engineer in the AI era.

cos_cname: 生成式 AI 系統設計與實務
cos_ename: Design and Practice of Generative AI Systems
dep_ename: Department of Industrial Engineering and Management
crs_outline:
本課程聚焦於生成式 AI 在企業場域中的系統化設計與實務應用，課程內容從大型語言模型基礎出發，延伸至檢索增強生成（RAG）、Agentic Workflow、智能體系統、小型語言模型（SLM）部署，以及 SDD / TDD 導向的 AI 系統架構設計。
本課程不以單純操作生成式 AI 工具為目標，而是引導學生理解如何將語言模型整合至企業資料、流程、工具與資訊系統中，設計出可測試、可評估、可維護且具備實際落地價值的 AI 應用。
修課學生完成本課程後，應能：
○ 說明企業級生成式 AI 系統的基本架構，包括前端、後端、資料庫、向量庫、模型、API、權限與紀錄追蹤。
○ 建置可驗證的 RAG 系統，完成文件切分、Metadata 設計、Embedding、向量檢索、回答生成與來源引用。
○ 設計可使用工具、呼叫 API、查詢資料庫與執行流程的 Agent / 智能體工作流。
○ 比較 LLM、SLM、地端模型與雲端模型在成本、延遲、資料安全與維運上的取捨。
○ 運用 SDD / TDD 思維撰寫 AI 系統規格、測試案例與驗收標準。
○ 完成一個具備資料檢索、工具呼叫、流程控制、測試驗證與部署規劃的企業 AI 系統原型。

crs_outline:
1.期中考階段從基礎財務管理理論出發，搭配板書示範與講授財務實務資料，介紹報酬、風險、事件研究、房地產投資的理論基礎。接著，本課程闡釋財務管理資本資產定價理論，培養同學資本資產評價的實力，課程進行中，老師提供國家考試高考或證券投資顧問事業證券投資分析人員相關試題，分析學生畢業後，財務管理就業與考試趨勢分析，老師進而板書解題示範引導作答方向，學生從做中學領悟投資意涵，幫助學生建立財務管理的基本觀念。
2.期末報告階段老師循序漸進引導學生實作事件研究，奠定投資實務與學術論文撰寫基礎，進行財務與人工智慧的跨域教學，強調財務、產業分析和人工智慧跨域學習，釐清人工智慧深入影響各種產業，投資人選擇投資標的應考量人工智慧，才能有效衡量公司價值，避免錯估企業的成效與價值，課程進行中老師也會穿插真實的案例實際教導同學實務上財務管理的運作。
3.課程安排的學術論文，從永續發展文獻可看出財務管理課程因應全球永續發展目標的潮流，教導學生投資標的需順勢選取致力綠色製程與綠色產品創新的企業(諸如台積電等)，投資選股前事先參考會計師認證的「永續發展、社會責任暨公司治理報告書」，判別企業的綠色績效，選擇前景良好的公司進行投資，提升長期投資的獲益。
4.本課程以財務學出發，帶學生領悟實務界預測公司股價的基礎，以數學證明的方式，讓學生了解證券金融產業每股盈餘比率(本益比)設定在20的理論基礎，以利同學投資理財之應用，理論與實務結合。

crs_outline: Strategic management is concerned with managing the competitive position (including the general environment, industry and market structure, and organizational strengths and weaknesses) and long-term development of the business enterprise. This course aims to relate the principles and issues addressed in the various functional business areas to introduce an integrated concept of management and provide an understanding of the relationship between theory and practice in general management. The course will lead students into two main areas which must be analyzed in order to formulate and implement a well-conceived strategy: the external environment of the firm (the industry context), and the internal environment of the firm (its resources and capabilities). Some of the key topics covered include: (1) exploring why and how good strategic management increases business performance, (2) the application of a set of analytical frameworks, (3) analyzing the reasons for the success and failure of a firm, and (4) the methods of developing an effective competitive strategy and executing it competently. The teaching materials include lectures, case analyses, and independent readings.

crs_outline:
Course Description:
This course introduces financial accounting steps by steps to students. Accounting involves the entire process of identifying, recording and communicating business events. First of all, this course interprets accounting principles, ethics and the role of accounting in business environments. Next, we instruct students to employ information of accounting statements to assess corporate financial status, operation achievements and cash flows. Another feature of this course is to lead students to understand accounting process and to teach them accounting practices such as agency problems and earnings management, so as to spark students’ interests in accounting. Our study of accounting will provide students insight into financial statement analysis, so students can successfully uncover business questions through analyzing accounting information.

Objectives/Goals:
Students in this course can learn following issues. 
1.  Understand the basic accounting principles and assumptions of recording enterprise transactions.
2.  Realize the procedure of the accounting cycle from entry journals, T-accounts to the preparation of accounting statements.
3.  Prepare income statements, statements of financial position, and cash flow statement. 
4.  Learn about current issues that the accounting field is concerned about, such as expected credit loss and gain, research development, and further discuss present controversies of accounting standards.
5.  Realize accounting practices and analyze financial statements through case studies.

crs_outline: This course is designed to develop graduate students’ academic research and scholarly writing skills in the field of global business. The course provides systematic guidance on the process of conducting academic research, including identifying research questions, reviewing and synthesizing literature, developing theoretical frameworks, designing research methodologies, analyzing data, and writing academic papers suitable for conference presentations and journal submissions. Through readings of high-quality journal articles, discussions of research design, writing workshops, and academic projects, students will learn how to critically evaluate existing research and contribute to scholarly conversations in global business. Particular emphasis is placed on academic writing, argument development, theoretical contribution, and research ethics. By the end of the course, students will be able to develop a research proposal and produce a well-structured academic paper that meets the standards of graduate-level research.

crs_outline:
量化研究方法旨在介紹以量化研究為基礎之論文結構建立，包含研究思維生成、問題定義、模型設計與仿真實驗結果檢驗及分析。幫助學生確立論文研究主題暨一系列之研究過程建立與驗證，並促進主要獨立研究思維生成以及未來在不同領域之工作所需之定量分析方法知識。
本課程的目的在於提供: 1) 基礎量化研究方法之認識，2) 基礎統計學理論知識了解，3) 淺薄資料科學理論知識了解。本課程完成後，學生將掌握量化研究的基本知識及其相關資料科學思維，並進一步了解其在不同領域之實務應用。

cos_ename: Pattern Recognition of Smart Healthcare Data
crs_outline: The intent of this course aims to effectively address the pattern recognition problems of smart healthcare data by developing high performance machine learning models. In the 21th century, the medical data are generated by a variety of elaborated medical diagnostic machines, and these medical data are usually complicated with the uncertainty. Through addressing the pattern recognition problem of medical data, the pattern or hidden information can be positively discovered from medical raw data, and it can further bring a good diversity of contribution to smart healthcare, such as key symptom identification and clinical decision support. Through giving a brief concept of machine learning modeling, this also provides real works to accumulate the practical experience of addressing the pattern recognition problem of smart healthcare data. Upon completion of this course, students will have the rudimentary knowledge of machine learning and the corresponding skills to address the pattern recognition problem of smart healthcare data.

研究所課程_一般研究所_管理學院_ITM(科技管理研究所)[碩]
crs_outline:
科學技術創新的進步是如此地快速, 人類的反應和適應力, 社會和道德、經濟和企業、政治和法規等等都跟不上腳步, 時間一久, 全都亂了套, 到底 ”科技創新” 要將人類帶往何處? 這門課就要探討這個問題。
夲課的重點是給予學生近十年內最新的科技創新發展和對人類歷史發展的新看法。希望學生在認知上能有所啟發、探索、思考、判斷、選擇和為什麼。大學研究所的教育在於強化學生深入分析批判、綜合思考、創新思維且擁有清晰表達自己理念的能力，使他們終身受益、擁有最寶貴的技能。 
所以這門課的重點在於學生勇於表達自己的想法和問題。基本上夲課要求學生:平時的出席率、課堂Quizzes上寫出自己的看法和參與課堂上的討論。 
夲課程聚焦在最新的科技創新和知識的更新, 領域包括半導體、無線通訊、物聯網、車聯網、自動化、中美貿易科技戰、AI人工智慧、人體醫學、地球暖化、人類發展史等方向, 每方向將會選擇一些相關子題來探討。
本學期的重點放在：科技管理、人類發展史、中美貿易戰：半導體產業及A I人工智慧發展、人體醫學。

crs_outline:
This course aims to analyze technology management literature by first-principle approach. Academic papers are deconstructed into systematic components, e.g. external Environment, literature analysis leading to the argument, what is the problem? what is literature gap? what does this research contribute to the scholarly literature by addressing the problem, etc. The deconstruction of research paper is associated with subsequent reconstruction process to develop new knowledge.

The objective of this course is to help student build up a reservoir of “first principles” in technology management and associate those principles with different fields. Students can learn how to deconstruct knowledge into fundamental principles then reconstruct the fundamental principles in new fields to facilitate efficient learning transfer and knowledge recombination.

memo: [English Medium Course]
crs_outline:
Course Descriptions and Objectives: This course examines digital technology innovation from both managerial and research perspectives. It introduces key theoretical frameworks and empirical research related to digital innovation, digital transformation, and technology management. Through lectures, academic readings, case discussions, and research-oriented assignments, students will learn how digital technologies influence innovation processes and business ecosystems. The course will also introduce major research themes and methodologies used in digital innovation research, helping students understand how scholars study digital technologies and their impacts on organizations and industries. Upon completion of the course, students will be able to: 
•	Understand the role of digital technologies in innovation and organizational transformation. 
•	Analyze digital innovation using major theoretical frameworks in technology management research.
•	Review and evaluate academic research related to digital innovation. 
•	Understand common research methods used in digital innovation studies. 
•	Develop research ideas related to digital technology innovation and management.

crs_outline:
本課程為陽明交大管理學院多位教授與台積電(TSMC)多位主管合作開授之課程。課程以全球觀點介紹半導體產業重要管理議題。課程由陽明交大管理學院教授們與台積電主管們共同授課，開放管院碩博士班學生(不含在職專班學生)選課。課程結合理論與實務，學生也將在課程中學習世界一流的半導體公司台積電第一手的經營管理實務。課程將提供學生以下知識：
1. 半導體產業的產業結構、營運模式，以及參與廠商等。
2. 半導體產業的需求預測、資源規劃，以及生產規劃議題。
3. 半導體產業中的數位轉型(digital transformation)。
4. 半導體產業中的智慧製造與自動化物料系統。
5. 半導體產業中的供應鏈與物流管理
6. 半導體產業中的雇主品牌管理
7. 半導體產業ESG相關議題(多元、平等、共融、職場健康等)
8. 半導體產業的人才發展

cos_ename: The Application of Computer Algorithms in Transportation
dep_cname: 運輸與物流管理學系交通運輸碩博士班
crs_outline: The course aims to introduce the computation concepts used in analyzing transportation problems. It includes the following topics: C++ / Python language tutorial, data structures, elementary and advanced searching & sorting algorithms, graph algorithms (Dijkstra's Algorithm, Augmenting Path algorithm, Prim's Algorithm, Kruskal's Algorithm, etc.) and algorithm design techniques (Divide-and-Conquer Algorithms, Dynamic Programming, Branch-and-Bound Technique, Meta-Heuristics). Applications and case studies presented include transportation-related problems (Shortest Path Problems, Maximum Flow, Minimum Spanning Tree, Facility Location Problems, Traveling Salesman Problem, maintenance, logistics analysis etc.). After taking the course, students are expected to be able to solve transportation problems using computer algorithms with C++/ Python language.

crs_outline: The purpose of this course is to provide the enrolled students with the knowledge of transportation risks, especially for operational and safety risks. The ultimate goal is to equip them with the professional skills and capability of managing transportation risks. The main theme is to emphasize the applications of risk management concepts and principles to transportation planning, operation, control, and management. The first half of this course will be discussing the fundamental aspects of risk management, including the basic concepts, principles, and applications for operational and safety risks. The second half will be focusing on transportation risk management-related research and modeling. The course consists of the following modules: 1) risk management modeling, 2) interactions among institute, environment, transportation mode and operator, 3) human factor, 4) safety management system, and 5) transportation security risk management. After finishing this course, the students are expected to have a better understanding of the complicated issues concerning transportation risk management and possess, the necessary knowledge, tools, and techniques for tackling transportation risk management problems.

3.	點名：現場掃QR-code簽到，簽到連結投影在講台布幕，只開放10分鐘(1:20-1:30)，每次上課都是新的連結，不重複使用。簽到完成會自動寄送副本給作答者，請務必確認資料無誤&及時簽到，遲到視為缺席。

每次演講，請於隔日中午12:00前將心得報告上傳至E3，且原創性比對之相似度必須低於10%。超過時間系統將關閉，亦不受理補交作業。缺交作業&相似度高於10%視為缺席。
 報告內容：中英文皆可，內容1至2頁A4紙，請寫上日期_學號_姓名。

2. 	Turnitin 原創性比對：
報告禁止抄襲或不當引用，助教會設定於E3系統收報告時自動做Turnitin原創性比對，若相似度超過10%，則當次以「缺課」論。
3.	QA：
演講期間與講者詢問與演講內容直接相關的問題，該堂課向助教登記學號姓名，可抵免該次作業。每次演講允許五位學生抵免作業。
4.	跨校選課者，請與本校課務組申請E3系統權限，於E3上傳心得報告，助教會設定於E3系統內收報告時自動做Turnitin原創性比對。
5.	每學期一次的心理諮商師演講/宣導，該次演講不需繳交報告。
6.	專題演講課程以「通過」或「不通過」為成績。

由於演講廳投影及擴音設備極易受到電子訊號的干擾，上課期間請關閉無線網路連線。

cos_cname: 創新與創業理論研討(二)
memo: 開放大三大四選修。
crs_outline: Innovation and entrepreneurship is increasingly the source of sustainable competitive advantage for firms in the global knowledge economy. In the past several decades, scholars have provided sufficient understanding of the innovation and entrepreneurship management. This course aims to systematically introduce the theory of innovation and entrepreneurship to provide students a clear picture of what current literature has done and what we may go. Through studying a series of classical papers and readings, students are expected to develop an understanding of what are the theories and how can they be used in the research of the innovation and entrepreneurship fields. The teaching materials include journal papers published in the leading journals.

dep_cname: 資訊管理與財務金融系財務金融博士班
crs_outline:
企業從事合併與收購以追求外部成長，其必須結合公司理財、證券市場、策略管理、財務會計與財經法律的知識與人才，因此合併與收購所承擔的風險並不亞於內部成長。本課程以公司理財（Corporate Finance）理論為基礎，並且強化購併個案介紹和評述，以及公司評價模型的分析。課程內容包含：購併程序、風險管理、個案分析、due diligence、購併策略、公司評價、接管與反接管措施。
課程特點：
包含併購的主要構面，並且有非常多的個案讓同學更瞭解各章的精髓與實務運作。
同學隨著課程的進行，撰寫M&A的計畫書與各個分析，可以達到Learning by doing的優點，並且可獲得全方面評估M&A的能力。

memo: [English Medium Course]
cos_ename: Science, Technology, Governance and Responsible Innovation
crs_outline:
當前全球面臨社會不平等加劇、科技發展帶來的倫理與治理挑戰，以及永續發展壓力，如何透過創新治理機制促進更公平且負責任的科技發展，已成為學術界與政策制定者關注的核心議題。本課程聚焦於負責任創新（Responsible Innovation, RI）、區域創新(Regional Innovation)與包容導向創新（Inclusive Innovation）的理論與實踐，培養學生對科技發展與社會變遷的理解及應用能力。課程內容導入包容導向創新、聯合國永續發展目標（Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs）、以及負責任創新的核心概念，透過探索式教學場域，讓學生深入理解科技治理的挑戰與可能解方。本課程不僅關注科技創新的社會影響，也探討政策規範、企業治理、社會責任及創新生態系統的建構，使學生能夠理解如何透過科技與創新實踐促進社會可持續發展。本課程將從負責任創新的理論基礎出發，參考英國研究與創新局（UK Research and Innovation, UKRI）所定義的負責任創新AREA架構，包括預期（Anticipate）、反思（Reflect）、參與（Engage）、行動（Act）。透過系統化的研究方法與實務應用，學生將學習如何在科技創新與社會發展的交互作用中納入永續社會責任考量，分析科技創新可能帶來的影響，探索其在經濟、社會、治理等層面的變遷，並透過開放對話與多元利害關係人的參與機制，設計出能夠回應社會需求的創新方案。
The primary objectives of this course include training in key research methods in the field of technology management and an in-depth review of important theoretical and practical literature in technology innovation management. A particular focus is placed on understanding and applying responsible innovation to design solutions that address diverse societal needs, thereby enhancing the fairness and accessibility of technological applications. The course will build upon the theoretical foundations of responsible innovation, drawing on the UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) definition of responsible innovation through the AREA framework: Anticipate, Reflect, Engage, and Act. By integrating systematic research methods with practical applications, students will learn to incorporate social responsibility considerations into technology innovation management. The course will guide students in analyzing the potential impacts of technological innovations, exploring their possible economic, social, and environmental consequences while emphasizing open dialogue and stakeholder engagement throughout the research and innovation process.

crs_outline:
This course explores the intersection of sustainability, innovation, and entrepreneurship, with a focus on how organizations design and implement strategies that address sustainability challenges while creating new business opportunities. Students will examine key theories and frameworks related to sustainable innovation, entrepreneurial strategy, and value creation. The course also emphasizes research perspectives and research methods in the study of sustainability and innovation. Through academic literature discussions, case analyses, and research-based projects, students will develop the ability to critically analyze sustainability-driven innovation and design research projects in this field.

Upon completion of the course, students will be able to: 
•	Understand the role of sustainability in innovation and entrepreneurial strategy. 
•	Analyze sustainable innovation using major theoretical frameworks in technology and innovation management research.
•	Review and evaluate academic research related to sustainable innovation and entrepreneurship. 
•	Understand common research methods used in sustainability and innovation studies.
•	Develop research ideas related to sustainable innovation and entrepreneurial strategy.

crs_outline:
開始上課日期: 待定
***公布博士班報告順序日期: 待定，第一週報告者請於(日期待定)前將所挑選的期刊論文寄給各組授課老師進行審核是否合適於課堂上報告，(日期待定)將公布碩士班報告順序(開學加退選結束後)，第一次報告日: 待定***
博士班學生請選擇一篇主要的論文，"以及三四篇重要的相關文獻"，做一個完整的介紹。如果選擇 review，請務必把來龍去脈講解清楚，並且針對最新或最重要的一篇研究做深入探討。報告時間約40分鐘，討論問題約15分鐘。修這堂課的博班同學請每堂課都提出問題與講者討論。

1.限挑選發表在四年內(2022-2026)的期刊論文，以英文報告。 
2.報告之期刊論文以“計算”類相關的期刊論文報告，論文主題需挑選與「生物資訊」或與「生物醫學」類相關的論文報告。 
3.限挑選「非自己實驗室」 發表的論文報告，指導教授實驗室發表論文可供參考與討論。
4.所挑選的期刊論文需於2週前寄給各組授課老師進行審核是否合適於課堂上報告 (逾期寄送論文將於C項出席分數中扣分)。
5.上傳所挑選之論文至E3上討論區的 "article for presentation"。
6.論文報告前先以2分鐘中文概述論文內容(外籍生可免)。


First class: 待定
***The presentation order for Ph.D. students will be announced on:待定. Those scheduled to present in the first week must send the journal articles they have selected to all instructors of their respective groups by 待定 for review to determine their suitability for the class presentation. The presentation order for Master's students will be announced on 待定, after the course registration and add/drop period has ended.****** First presentation date: 待定 ***

Please select a main article and three or four important and related references to give a comprehensive introduction. If the article is a review paper, please make sure to explain the contexts clearly, and make thorough discussion according to the latest or most important references. The presentation will be about 40 minutes, and the discussion section is about 15 minutes. Every Ph.D. student attending this class must ask questions to the speaker(s) and join the discussion. The chosen articles should meet the following criteria: 

1. Published within four years (2022-2026) and in the English language written.
2. The Journal of the article should belong to the category of " computational biology", and the topic of the article itself should be related to "Bioinformatics" or "Biomedicine".
3. The selected article shall not be published from your own laboratory, but the papers published by your advisor can be added to the discussion.
4. The article should be sent to all instructors of their respective groups 2 weeks before your presentation for review to determine its suitability for the class report. Failure to send the article on time will result in a deduction of points from the attendance grade (score "C").
5. Upload the selected article to "article for presentation" in forum on E3.  
6. Before your presentation, please summarize the article in Chinese for 2 minutes (foreign students are not included).

專題研討課程分為上、下二學期，並以分組討論方式進行研討。上學期以研讀並報告與同學論文主題相關之國內外文獻為主，下學期則以報告每位同學碩士論文之內容與進度以及預期成果為主要研討重點。下學期課程目標如下：
1.	訓練並提昇學生表達與上台報告之能力：包括問題的描述，解決問題的方法與過程，預期成果等。並於過程訓練學生之邏輯與臨場反應以及台風等。
2.	訓練並提昇學生主持專題研討之能力：每週研討會將指定兩位同學負責專題研討的流程與串場，模擬國際研討會之形式，訓練學生主持與掌控會場情境之能力。
3.	提昇學生問問題之能力：研討過程中要求學生提問問題，訓練學生提問問題之能力。
分享研究之成果：讓與會的同儕能夠清楚了解彼此的研究問題，分享研究成果。長遠的影響是作為未來職場上的合作與人才推薦的參考以及人際網路的基礎。

memo: (不受理紙本加簽, 校際選修除外) 學生須出席第1堂課，經授課教師同意者可登記加選，應藝所優先
cos_ename: Experimental Media Art and Design Practice
crs_outline: 本課程聚焦於實驗媒體藝術與設計的創作實踐，結合創作方法論與當代實驗媒體表現技術，引導學生跨領域發展個人創作計畫。課程初期將介紹媒體藝術的歷史脈絡與經典案例，涵蓋互動藝術、生成藝術、人工智慧與資料藝術等類型，提供理論與美學基礎。中期進入創作方法論的訓練，包括敘事設計、原型製作、科技整合與觀眾互動策略。後期以工作坊形式進行創作實作與作品發表，教師將以個別指導與同儕討論方式，陪伴學生深化創作內容，最終完成具批判性與創新性的媒體藝術作品。本課程取代之前「創新媒材課」，有修此課的同學不用來重複修課。

crs_outline:
一、出席規定：
1. 實體授課，地點在博愛校區賢齊館1F聯強國際會議廳，若因臨床責任需求，學生得選擇以線上視訊方式聽講至多7次。
2. 演講時間表：開學公告於E3教學平台、系所網頁（開學前及每次演講前一週皆會公告於系所[最新消息]）。
3. 點名：現場掃QR-code簽到，簽到連結只開放10分鐘(1:20-1:30)，投影在講台小布幕，每次上課都是新的連結，不重複使用。請務必準時簽到，遲到視為缺課。(線上簽到連結會公布於視訊聊天室，規定同現場簽到，只開放10分鐘，遲到視為缺課)
4. 若缺課1次會扣除1次線上聽講機會，即缺課次數加上線上聽講之次數不得大於7次。
5. 缺課3次(含)以上（也就是最多只能缺席2次），學期成績以不及格論。

二、報告繳交規則：
1. 每次演講，請於隔日中午12:00前將心得報告上傳至E3，超過時間系統將關閉不得繳交，亦不受理補交作業。缺交作業視為缺課。
2. 詢問講者與演講內容直接相關的問題，可以抵免該次作業。
3. 每次演講允許五位學生抵免作業。
4. 報告禁止抄襲或不當引用，助教會設定於 E3 系統內收報告時自動做 Turnitin 原創性比對，若相似度請勿超過 10%，則當次以「缺課」論。同學繳交報前請先以 Turnitin 自行檢查，但繳交報告時請勿附上比對結果。
報告內容：中英文皆可，內容1至2頁A4紙，請寫上姓名-學號-日期。
報告檔名：日期_學號_姓名 (例：0928_410355XXX_傅攀達)
5. 跨校選課者，請與本校課務組申請E3系統權限，於E3上傳心得報告，助教會設定於E3系統內收報告時自動做Turnitin原創性比對。
6. 每學期一次的心理諮商師演講/宣導，該次演講不需繳交報告。
7. 專題演講課程以「通過」或「不通過」為成績。
三、課程公約
由於演講廳投影及擴音設備極易受到電子訊號的干擾，上課期間請關閉無線網路連線。
未經同意請勿側錄及散播演講內容。

四、課程助教聯絡方式
沈亮彣
邱昉柔

crs_outline:
本課程採實體授課，本學期將分兩組上課，依照學號來分組，偶數同學加入Ａ組，奇數同學加入Ｂ組，請同學們選擇正確的課程。
(偶數) A組授課老師: 待定 ; Room 302 課程編號: 430103
(奇數) B組授課老師: 待定 ; Room 310 課程編號: 430114
第一次上課時間: 待定 
碩士班報告順序公布(開學加退選結束後): 待定 
*** 第一次報告日: 待定  ***
請選擇一篇論文報告，可與自己研究相關或無關。若與自己研究相關，可同時介紹自己的研究並與此篇論文做比較與討論。報告時間約20分鐘，討論問題約10分鐘。

1.限挑選發表在四年內(2022-2026)的期刊論文，以英文報告。
2.報告之期刊論文以“計算”類相關的期刊論文報告，論文主題需挑選與「生物資訊」或與「生物醫學」類相關的論文報告。
3.限挑選「非自己實驗室」 發表的論文報告，指導教授實驗室發表論文可供參考與討論。
4.***Update!! 所挑選的期刊論文需於3週前寄給各組授課老師進行審核是否合適於課堂上報告 (逾期寄送論文將於C項出席分數中扣分)。***
5.上傳所挑選之論文至E3上討論區的 "article for presentation"。
6.***New!! 將完整的報告錄製成影片(包含投影片以及本人口說, 17-23分鐘)，在報告的前一天之前上傳至E3(逾期寄送影片將於D項教授分數中扣分) 。***
7.論文報告前先以2分鐘中文概述論文內容(外籍生可免)。

This course will be conducted in person; all students taking these courses (course numbers: 430103, 430104) will be divided into two groups according to their student numbers. Students with odd numbers join group A, and even numbers join group B. For master students, please select the correct course, 430103 or 430104.
(EVEN) Group A: Room 302 (Course Number: 430103)
(ODD) Group B: Room 310 (Course Number: 430114)
First class: 待定
The presentation order for Master's students will be announced on: 待定 after the course registration and add/drop period has ended.
*** First presentation date: 待定 ***
Please select an article, it can rather be related or unrelated to your own research. If it is related to your own research, you can also introduce and compare the article with your own research. The time for the presentation is about 20 minutes, and the discussion section will be 10 minutes. The chosen articles should meet the following criteria:

1. Published within four years (2022-2026) and in the English language written.
2. The Journal of the article should belong to the category of " computational biology", and the topic of the article itself should be related to "Bioinformatics" or "Biomedicine".
3. The selected article shall not be published from your own laboratory, but the papers published by your advisor can be added to the discussion.
4. *** Update!! The article should be sent to all professors 3 weeks before your presentation date. Failure to send the article on time will result in a deduction of points from the attendance grade (score "C"). ***
5. Upload the selected article to "article for presentation" in forum on E3.
6. *** New!! Upload the presentation video, which should be 17-23 minutes long, including both slides and oral content, one day before your presentation date. Failure to send the video on time will result in a deduction of points from the professors’ grade (score ”D"). ***
7. Before your presentation, please summarize the article in Chinese for 2 minutes (foreign students are not included).

crs_outline: 「跨媒介視覺設計」為視覺設計面對跨領域的研討課程，基於「媒介即訊息」的觀點，設計工作者要處理的不只是內容本身，而是巧用媒介，更深刻地塑造思維、創造文化與掌握他人的行動方式。媒介可以是任何形式的傳播工具，例如口語表達、文字符號、繪畫與影像、印刷媒體、電子媒體、社交媒體平台等。跨媒介的呈現的對於受眾來說極度重要，也同時影響創作者在對於設計的各種轉化與表述的功力。對此時代的設計工作者，若缺乏了正視媒介的視野，他們的作品將難以與世界真正對話。本課程提供設計相關工作者必備的鑑賞能力，通透的識讀任何媒介，無論是對語言、文字、圖像、影片，乃至社群、互動裝置、影音平台，都可以洞見其隱含的特定語法與權力關係，在此基礎上，將知識導入設計工作與作品之中。

crs_outline:
This course is designed to draw students into the disciplines and challenges for the contemporary issues of global marketing. It provides an introduction to global marketing, looks at the global marketing environment, discusses global strategy, explains the global marketing mix, and concludes with the efforts of managing the global market. Lessons are also hoped to bring data science into real implementation of key terms and issues, especially in STP analysis (statistical test), product strategy (conjoint analysis), cross selling (association rule mining), sales forecasting (moving average, regression, time series), and decision analysis.

For anyone involved in international marketing, and those seeking the kinds of strategies needed to enter the global marketplace, this course should be able to offer some necessary fundamentals of related theoretical analysis and problem resolution.

crs_outline: 本課程為針對產品設計為應用方向所開設之入門設計運算與數位製造整合訓練，以產品設計背景或對設計運算如何應用在產品設計有興趣之同學為主要對象。同學將學習以 Rhino 3D V8 為主要環境之視覺化編程建模工具 Grasshopper，與同學既有的 3D 幾何建模知識融合，並運用程式運算中固有的邏輯判斷、廻圈、法則、亂數、物理模擬等觀念技巧，來建構自動化參數設計程序，以快速生成人工建模所無法達到的複雜產品曲面皮層模型，同時利用程式的自動化及運算效率，得以快速產生大量多元化的衍生成果及提昇探索設計可能性的效率。

請選擇一篇論文報告，可與自己研究相關或無關。若與自己研究相關，可同時介紹自己的研究並與此篇論文做比較與討論。報告時間約20分鐘，討論問題約10分鐘。

crs_outline:
課程探討混合實境及虛擬實境之構築元素，強調3D虛擬世界之視覺意象及美感技法，試圖創造獨特奇幻之視覺美術風格，進而強化虛構非實境之沈浸感體驗及想像維度。

課程技術層面結合高斯潑濺(3DGS)、AI coding assistant (Github Copilot)、AI生成模型、3D素材庫進行三維空間場景設計，並以遊戲引擎Unreal Engine或TouchDesigner為開發工具進行場景運鏡體驗與互動設計。理論層面，則以李飛飛教授之空間智慧(Spatial Intelligence)，及經典戲劇理論，例如布魯克《空的空間》作為討論框架，試圖探索在AI生成世界下人類的嶄新空間感知，以及在虛擬世界增強群體共感經驗。

實作三大主軸，(ㄧ) 結合Marble AI, Luma AI, Apple Sharp AI, TripoSplat AI 進行虛擬場景設計。(二) 以3DGS為出發輔以Github Copilot，進行風格化場景設計(non-photorealistic scenic design)及視覺特效(post-process effect：Bloom、Filmic Tonemaping、Color grading、Vignette、Depth of field、Lens Flare...)等等表現技法提升美術質地。(三) 加上模擬機制、氣候狀態、運鏡與互動等。

crs_outline:
大眾對於醫療品質的追求一直是各種先進技術導入醫療場域的強烈動機來源，其中，3D掃瞄設備技術在近年快速普及，使得人體體表逆向掃瞄變得更加容易實現，這種非接觸式且精準地建構人體數位模型的光學技術逐漸被討論用來替代傳統醫療製作各類穿戴式輔具、護具、矯正器的實體翻模方法。而同樣也在快速普及的3D列印由於近年來成本降低、品質提昇、效率加快，也逐漸被討論到用來進行客製化醫療用品或少量製造產品的可能性，使得原本因無法達到生產經濟規模門檻的產品得到落實的可能。

基於上述背景，本課程由兩個產品設計開發單元構成，第一單元為應用人體3D掃瞄與3D列印進行 Patient-Matched Device 客製化穿戴裝置之製作，第二單位為針對需求量少的診斷或復健用品進行以 3D列印及少量製造為前提的設計開發。

第一單元Patient-Matched Device 客製化穿戴裝置之設計製作，將教授學生針對身體特定部位，如頭、四肢、軀幹來設計客製化之穿戴裝置，課程中將運用手持式3D掃瞄器對所設定之身體局部進得體表網格模型，並運用教師提供之程式來生成可穿戴的鏤空薄殻結構，最終運用3D列印將之實體。課程中，學生將習得此一數位化工作流程並發掘可能潛在問題。

第二單元分為兩個主題A、B，主題A延續學生在第一單元所製作的客製化穿戴薄殻作為載體，由於此載體長時間配戴於使用者身上，因此獲得貼近其身體收集生理或環境數據的可能，例如偵測皮膚腫脹壓力、局部體表溫濕度、肢體活動彎曲角度等、所處環境空氣品質等等，其偵測不一定為醫療目的，可以延伸為推測設計或互動藝術創作之面向。因此學生可依據其設計目的來選擇適用的偵測元件，在載體作植入元件設計，並驗證是否滿足其預期目的、收集數據或觸發互動之可行性。主題B則為針對治療復健過程中使用之產品的IOT與3D列印化設計，這些產品中有些會用來幫助治療師判斷患者手、脚、眼、腦的活動效率，例如三分鐘登階測試或單手及手指靈活度評估測試器材，由於這些產品的市場需求量少，製造商缺乏開發生產意願，因此通常以簡易、低成本器材型態為主。然而這些產品具有收集大數據之潛力，因此主題B為透過電子元件與Arduino將這些產品轉化為自動化且能收集第一手數據的原型設計，並以 3D列印思維克服量產門檻。

cos_cname: 數位科技陶瓷製造與創作
memo: (不受理紙本加簽, 校際選修除外) 應藝所優先；上課教室：人二館教學工場 HB13
cos_ename: Digital Technology in Ceramic Fabrication and Creative Practice
crs_outline:
本課程以陶瓷材料為主，透過陶土與釉藥作為主要材料，並以科技輔助陶藝創作為核心概念進行教學。課程目標除了讓同學理解傳統陶瓷製作方式，如手捏、拉坯成型，以及工業化生產中常見的石膏灌漿與旋坯等工法之外，也進一步引導同學認識如何運用數位科技工具輔助陶藝創作與製造流程。

相較於傳統陶瓷在打樣或量產時，往往需要經歷開模製作與反覆溝通修正等繁複程序，科技工具的介入能夠有效縮短製作流程，並快速建立多樣化的作品形式與可能性。本課程旨在使修課同學理解科技輔助製造在陶藝創作與製造上的便利性，並藉此拓展對陶瓷創作方法的手段，期待激發更多跨越傳統製程的創作可能性。

課程分成以下幾個單元：
第一單元：雷射切割與陶盤製造
透過 Grasshopper 進行紋理與圖樣設計，並運用雷射切割技術製作模具，完成陶盤的製作流程，理解數位設計如何轉換為實體陶瓷作品。
第二單元：CNC 銑床與花磚製造
使用 Grasshopper 建立數位模型，並透過電腦數值控制（CNC）銑床進行加工，製作具客製化特徵的陶瓷花磚，認識數位製造於陶瓷產製中的應用方式。
第三單元：3D 列印與馬克杯製造
利用 Grasshopper 設計表面肌理，透過陶瓷 3D 列印技術製作杯體。同時結合石膏模具灌漿方式製作杯把，使同學理解數位製造與傳統陶瓷產業製程之間的整合與應用。

cos_cname: 十六、十七世紀歐洲視覺文化
memo: 1.視覺文化研究所課程結構發展重點一：近代視覺藝術。2.本課程同意開放大學部學生選修，但學生需與授課老師面談同意後，始能以紙本加選的方式選修。
crs_outline:
課程概述與目標：
       十六與十七世紀歐洲面臨政治、宗教與文化變革，包括宗教改革與反宗教改革、宮廷文化的興起、全球貿易的擴張，以及科學知識的發展。這些變化促使西方視覺藝術蓬勃發展，產生嶄新的形式，展開多元的觀看方式。
        本課程為西方藝術與視覺文化入門課程，目的在介紹1500年至 1700年之間歐洲的視覺藝術，以義大利、北方歐洲、西班牙、法國與荷蘭共和國等地的繪畫、雕塑、建築、版畫與裝飾藝術為主要內容。首先以時時間軸介紹主要藝術形式與重要作品，藉此了解西洋視覺藝術發展的過程，亦將藝術視為一種深植於社會結構、物質條件與再現體系之中的文化實踐，通過性別、階級、種族、收藏等觀點，了解作品背後的視覺意涵。

       修課同學可習得十六十七世紀歐洲主要視覺藝術作品的產製、形式以及創作思維等等知識，培養視覺分析技巧，了解藝術家如何與當時代的社會對話，並思考這些作品如何融入二十一世紀的文化中，醞釀出嶄新的意義與價值。

cos_cname: 工藝設計中的視覺、物質與政治
memo: 1.視覺文化研究所課程結構發展重點三：近代視覺與技術。 2.本課程同意開放大學部學生選修，但學生需與授課老師面談同意後，始能以紙本加選的方式選修。
cos_ename: Visuality, Materiality and Politics in Design History
crs_outline:
在視覺文化研究領域中，工藝設計的歷史與其物質性（materiality）逐漸成為學者關注的重要議題之一。許多過往被歸類為裝飾藝術而常被排除於傳統藝術史研究之外的媒材形式（例如家具、壁紙、陶瓷與織品等），事實上承載了不同文化情境中的社會意義與歷史脈絡。本課程首先探討藝術史、視覺文化研究與物質文化研究等領域之間的方法與觀點，說明工藝設計在當代研究中的重要性。接著從十六世紀歐洲裝飾藝術的發展出發，逐步討論十八世紀的設計與製造、東西文化交流、藝術與工藝之間的界線、以及工業化時代「工藝」概念的形成。課程進一步延伸至工藝與帝國、民族認同、性別文化想像、工藝教育等議題，並探討二十世紀以降工藝在國家文化政策、女性主義實踐與數位文化中的新發展。

透過上述主題，本課程旨在引導學生理解工藝設計如何與文化認同、政治權力與社會價值交織，並培養學生從視覺文化與物質文化角度分析設計與工藝的能力。此外，課程亦包含手工藝實作與影像分享等學習活動，讓學生透過材料操作與創作經驗，實際體會手工製作的物質性與勞動過程，並進一步反思工藝在當代視覺文化與社群媒體中的呈現方式。藉由理論閱讀與實作經驗的結合，學生將能更全面地理解工藝設計在不同歷史與文化脈絡中的意義，以及其中所蘊含的各種政治性（politics）。

crs_outline:
本課程針對設計領域研究生，以創意和實務型研究、設計科學、運算思維為核心，試圖建立設計研究之基本認識與初步練習。課程內容包括設計研究基本認識、創意研究的研究方法、數位建築史觀、設計思維、數位與運算思維、研究倫理、設計研究提案練習等。學期後半段，分為設計研究組、學士後兩組分開教學，針對研究方向與研究案例進行研習與寫作練習。

Professional design development encompasses a diverse range of careers, spanning from the idealistic to the pragmatic and from the academic to the industrial. Regardless of the specific profession, the ability to conduct design research and possess knowledge of design science is becoming increasingly vital. In architectural schools, while digital media is widely utilized for design representation and simulations, and despite the vast amount of information available online, there remains a significant gap in our proficiency to make informed design decisions and identify emerging design challenges.

This course is designed to equip students with the skills and knowledge necessary for design research and thesis writing. Through a combination of lectures, discussions, and exercises, students will acquire the essential knowledge and skills needed. Part 1 of the course lays the foundational knowledge for all students. Part 2A is tailored for MS and MArch II students, focusing on advanced design research that emphasizes innovation. Part 2B is designed for MArch I students, concentrating on preparing them to craft a design thesis that encapsulates and curates their academic works.

本課程設立之目的在培養學生發展建築研究方面之進階能力。課程主要以師生討論的方式進行，透過對於相關領域之基礎知識、研究方法、以及研究方向之分析，輔佐學生釐清個人之研究主題、並建立相關之關鍵技術能力。此外，對於進行中之研究、以及相關之實作專案，進行集體討論與意見交換，以協助達成高品質實作型研究為目標。

The purpose of this course is to foster advanced abilities in students to conduct research in architecture. The course primarily involves discussions between faculty and students, aiming to assist students in clarifying their research topics and establishing relevant key technical skills through the analysis of foundational knowledge, research methods, and research directions in the field. Additionally, collective discussions and exchange of opinions are conducted for ongoing research and related practical projects, with the goal of achieving high-quality practice-based research.

crs_outline:
課程介紹：人之為人 (Being Human) —— 從生物載體到覺醒的自然人
一、 課程主題：重構「人」的完整性
在當代高等教育中，「人」往往被拆解為不同學科下的功能碎片。在生物學中，我們被視為精密的生化機器；在社會學中，我們是階級與體制下的角色；在資訊科學中，我們則成了一串可預測的數據。然而，在這些碎片化的知識背後，那個關於「我是誰」的終極追問卻往往被遺忘了。本課程旨在重構那份失落的「完整人類經驗」，帶領大家穿透「生物人」的物質智慧、認清「社會人」的故事枷鎖，最終尋回那個與宇宙天地共振的「自然人」本體。
二、 課程理念：在存在中遇見知曉
我們對世界的認識，往往受限於我們當下的狀態。本課程的核心理念在於打破「知識僅是資訊累積」的迷思，轉而探討一種「存在即知曉」（Being as Knowing）的可能性。
借用赫胥黎（Aldous Huxley）與西方神祕主義的洞見：一個人的認知深度，其實是他生命品質的函數。這意味著，當我們的心靈處於機械式的反應與混濁的睡眠中時，有些真相是無論讀多少書都無法觸碰的。因此，我們在課程中提倡一種「證悟」高於「解悟」的態度——解悟是研讀地圖，而證悟則是腳步的抵達。我們將練習一種「感知領悟」（Sense of Knowing），這不是枯燥的邏輯推演，而是一種全方位的直覺性領會。當我們試著提升自己的「存在狀態」，讓內在變得更清澈透明時，那些關於生命的終極答案，便會像水面下的礁石在潮退後顯現一樣，自然地從你的生命中彰顯出來。
三、 課程路徑：四個階段的生命實驗
1. 發現機械性（W2-W7）： 旅程從我們最親近的身體出發。我們將驚嘆於細胞間極致的合作智慧，並以此為鏡，透過哈拉瑞（Yuval Noah Harari）與薩波斯基（Robert Sapolsky）的視野，誠實地觀察自己如何被社會故事與生理本能所驅動。這是一個「覺察」的過程，練習在日常中認出那些「機械式睡眠」的時刻。
2. 普世智慧與轉向（W9-W11）： 接著，我們將跨越東西方，進入「長青哲學」與神祕主義的世界。這是一個向內尋找導航系統的階段，我們將嘗試透過審美直觀與良知，去感受那個超越感官、與宇宙本源相契合的時刻。這不是要學習新教條，而是要驗證那些古老智慧在當代生活中的真實性。
3. 多維整合與探索（W12-W14）： 以榮格（Carl Gustav Jung）學說與唯識學建立超越個體的意識模型後，我們將結合肯·威爾伯（Ken Wilber）的意識階梯與賽斯（Seth material）的多維實相論。我們將探討意識如何像光線一樣投影出我們所見的物質世界，並學習識別那些隱藏在生活細節中的「共時性」提示，理解生命在垂直演化與水平擴張間的壯闊景致。
4. 歸於終極自由（W15）： 旅程的終點，是關於「放下」。我們將實踐萊斯特·利文森（Lester Levenson）的釋放法，剝離那些我們自願承擔的限制與重擔。最終的目標並非獲得更多，而是回歸一種「成為你之所是」的純粹喜悅。
四、 結語：邀請你，成為知曉本身
「人之為人」不提供標準答案，而是提供一套邀請。我們希望這門課結束時，你帶走的不是一張寫滿筆記的紙，而是一個更敏銳、更有存在感的靈魂。當你提升了「存在」的品質，你本身就是那份知曉真理的容器。

cos_ename: Image of Time: Cinema and Temporality
crs_outline: Cinema, a so-called time-based art, was created by the technology of capturing and reproducing images sequentially. However, it is not just a film’s content, but its very form that is involved in the production of images which are influenced by and reflect upon concepts of time. By considering cinema’s social functions and its very medium with a focus in cinematic devices, this course engages with thinking via cinematic devices and images related to temporality, consideration of time as linear or non-linear, homogeneous or heterogenous, and reversible or irreversible. Adapting an approach of close-reading of film texts and engaging with writings by such major theorists on temporality as Nietzsche, Heidegger, Bergson, Benjamin, Levinas, Deleuze, and Stiegler, concepts of being, love, desire, identity, memory, and revenge will be explored.

crs_outline:
This course introduces students to the trajectory of Theatre Anthropology and Performance Studies from their proximity traceable to the "Théâtre d'Art" and its critical legacy. Given recent exhibits at the Venice Biennale manifest the trend of theater arts being incorporated into the genre of fine art, and performance in museums has been embraced by institutions and artists for decades, the line between the fine art and performing arts is increasingly blurred. The readings included in this seminar foreground important subjects in the development of Theater Anthropology in relation to Anthropology of Symbolism and Anthropology of Body in the 1970s and their later version of development in Performance Studies in the 1990s onward, in order to address their impacts on contemporary art and our understanding of essential concepts about humanity such as performativity, liminality, speech acts, et cetera.

As theater arts remain deeply connected to Philosophical Anthropology and its subject of what accounts for human nature—the unity and identity of human beings into their constituent elements, and meanings of life—they are closely aligned with the theoretical development in the Anthropological studies of ritual and performance, owing much to scholars such as Victor Turner and Clifford Geertz who had pioneered in the analysis of body and symbolism in movement. We will also dive into the works and lives of leading scholars and artists in the field, including Richard Schechner, Eugenio Barba, Antoni Artaud, Jerzy Grotowski, Peter Brooks, Diana Taylor, and Marilyn Ivy—whose work address important genres such as Tent Theatre and Little Theatre that are increasingly considered essential to the global art histories from the inter-Asian perspective. These experiments in forms and social engagements are paramount in framing the ways in which theater, performing arts, and fine arts are conceived today. They allow us to contemplate on the role of contemporary theater and performing arts’ critical engagement with sociopolitical issues.

課程概述
建築結構系統包含”結構系統”與”結構學”兩大內涵，是建築設計的基礎，也是各類建築國家考試必考之科目。完整的教學規畫須透過”建築結構系統(I)(II)”(分為兩學期，各為3學分)來闡述。
(A) "建築結構系統(I)”課程主要內容與目標 :
◎各類型結構系統與結構行為
包括框架、桁架、拱、板殼、薄膜、懸索、木造、磚石造、   RC造、鋼骨造及各類型建築物基礎之構成。
◎鋼筋混凝土與鋼骨結構設計基本概念與設計研判。
◎抗震結構、抗風結構、隔震消能結構。
◎結構系統與建築規劃設計之整合。
(B) "建築結構系統(II)”課程主要內容與目標 :
◎基本結構力學原理
◎結構力學與構件設計及結構行為之關聯性
◎與時事有關之建築結構問題。
課程目標
”建築結構系統(I)”課程主要課程目標 :
◎瞭解各類型結構系統與結構行為。
◎瞭解結構抗震、抗風
◎瞭解結構系統與建築規劃設計之整合。

crs_outline:
Foundation Drawing and Model Course for New M.Arch I Students
本課程適合學士後建築新生修習，從基本圖學原理到模型製作技巧，循序漸進地建立設計表現所需的基礎知識與實作能力。課程將於暑假期間密集進行，讓同學能在開學前建立紮實的空間圖學與模型操作能力。開學後則會視同學設計課程的進度與負荷，安排適當時段進行補充教學，以小型工作坊的形式，進一步熟悉各種建築表現技術與工具操作。

圖學部分的重點，在於建立三維空間與二維圖面之間的符號轉換能力與空間敏感度。課程內容涵蓋建築構件與牆體介面的硬體圖學表達、空間中的活動序列與空間感的詮釋方法，以及綜合圖說製作的技巧。每次課程會以雙主軸方式進行：一方面訓練基本圖學邏輯與繪圖精準度，另一方面讓學生運用不同媒材進行個人化的空間詮釋與視覺傳達練習。

模型操作則著重於「安全性、精準性、設計製造、模型表現」四大主題，從建築模型的製作原理到灌模、材料創作等技術引導，鼓勵學生探索不同材料的特性與加工方式，強化工藝能力，同時拓展設計表達的層次與想像力，為後續設計課程打下穩固的技術與美學基礎。

crs_outline:
從圍堵與禁制的高牆，到如影隨形的數位監控；從安全、平等與權利的屏障，到團結抵抗的前提；從認同與差異、包容與排除的界線，到多樣生命形式混雜交錯的空間……
什麼是邊界？邊界在哪裡？為何設立邊界？邊界如何作用？誰是邊界行動者？有哪些不同的邊界體驗？
在當代世界中，隨著邊界型態、技術、功能與行動者不斷演變與擴充，對於移動的調控也愈加複雜、隱微，甚至難以察覺。本課程將結合跨領域的理論文獻、案例分析與實地踏查，透過邊界及其相關概念，探討各種虛實交錯的邊界工法如何成為當代世界權力運作的重要機制與場域；同時，形形色色的人與非人的移動，又如何順應、迴避、鬆動、僭越既有的邊界結構，並引發新的邊界實踐。

dep_ename: Institute for Social Research and Cultural Studies
crs_outline:
本課程為文化研究之入門概論，以「人民／民眾／大眾」為核心主題，引領學生認識文化研究的主要理論取向與分析方法。「大眾」既是現代政治動員的對象、文化生產的受眾，也是媒介中介的主體，其概念本身即折射出文化研究跨學科、多向度的知識關懷。本課程藉由聚焦這一主題，帶領學生掌握文化研究的問題意識與核心論爭。
課程分三個單元展開。第一單元「諸民之辨」從政治哲學切入，辨析「人民」概念在現代語境中的多重形態——從無民到民粹，從民族自決到社會運動——揭示「民」作為政治主體的內在張力與歷史變遷。第二單元轉向文化史與文化社會學，透過Burke、Adorno、Bourdieu、Gramsci等人的經典文本，考察大眾文化如何在與精英文化的對立中被定義，如何成為霸權競逐的場域，以及如何在新自由主義治理下重塑主體性。第三單元「Mediating the Mass」則引入媒介理論，從海德格、班雅明、克拉考爾到霍爾、麥克魯漢、基特勒，探討媒介如何構成大眾感知與認同的基礎設施，並延伸至當代平台文化與粉絲經濟的討論。
三個單元雖各有理論重心，卻共享一個問題意識：面對「人民／民眾／大眾」這一充滿爭議的概念，文化研究如何以跨學科的視野，揭示其中複雜交織的權力關係、文化實踐與認同政治。修習本課程，學生將獲得進入文化研究領域的基本理論裝備與批判性閱讀能力。

crs_outline:
This course will introduce crucial theories in gender and sexuality studies to students. The course will start with classical texts and then proceed to contemporary theories in the field. In addition to theory, we will also read films, moving-image works, digital media arts, scripts of avant-garde and underground performances, memoirs or “biomythography,” and activist video works so that students can understand that the discipline of gender and sexuality studies is never born out of interests of researchers in the ivory tower. Instead, it is a field where scholars “do theory” with social commitments and utopian aspirations for social change while enduring social and political oppression and, in the meantime, creating new forms of socialities and relationalities. 

---
做為一個由被壓迫者集結與形塑而成的學術領域，性別研究一直是一個與當前社會脈絡與文化政治緊密勾連的學科。本課程以此作為立足點與出發點，向學生引介性別研究裡的重要理論與議題。課程會由較為古典的性別理論開始，之後進行至當代重要的理論與議題。除了閱讀理論，我們也會討論電影與動態影像作品、數位電影/藝術、前衛與地下表演劇本、回憶錄或自傳神話、以及藝術家和社會運動行動者的抗議性影像藝術或行為藝術等。如此，修課學生將會理解性別研究從來就不是象牙塔裡的追尋，也與流行或商品化等學術污名無關。相反的，它一直是一個受壓迫者為了求生存而集結與誕生的學術領域，也一直在不斷變動與更新的壓迫性環境裡思索與記憶少數群體的歷史與政治創傷，並同時形塑新型態的社會關係與社群。

memo: [English Medium Course]
cos_ename: Archipelagic East Asia: Empire, Body, and Spatial
dep_ename: Institute for Social Research and Cultural Studies
crs_outline:
This course explores the making of modern East Asia through the lenses of critical historiographical turns, archipelagic thinking, and the politics of embodiment. Moving beyond nation-centered narratives, the course examines how empire, colonial modernity, and shifting spatial imaginaries shaped lived experiences across Taiwan, Japan/Okinawa, Korean Peninsula, Hong Kong, and the wider Pacific world.
This course consists of three sections: (1)Archipelagic Turn, (2) Bodies under Empire (3) Spatializing East Asia. We begin by situating postwar intellectual transformations within the broader “cultural turn” in historical studies, drawing on Geoff Eley and debates on colonial modernity. The course then develops an “Archipelagic Turn,” engaging with the Black Atlantic, Pacific Rim discourses, and critiques of area studies to reconsider East Asia as a fluid, interconnected space rather than a fixed geopolitical entity.
The second section “Bodies under Empire” investigates how imperial power operated through hunger, health, reproduction, and racialization. Topics include starvation science and geopolitics, eugenics and total war, colonial governance in Taiwan and Hong Kong, and the Okinawan experience of the “Cycad Hell.” Here, the body becomes a crucial site where empire materializes through regulation, deprivation, and survival.
The final section “Spatializing East Asia” brings the course into direct dialogue with its central themes of empire, body, and spatial politics. Rather than treating war as a discrete event, this section examines how imperial power reorganizes space—through caves, camps, and infrastructures of confinement—and how these spaces, in turn, shape embodied experience. From the caves (gama) of Okinawa to prisoner-of-war camps in Southeast Asia, we explore how landscapes become technologies of survival, coercion, and memory. Engaging with the idea of a “liquid” East Asia, the course ultimately approaches the region not as a fixed geopolitical container but as an archipelagic formation—an interconnected yet fractured field shaped by imperial mobility, displacement, and contested spatial orders. By tracing the entanglement of bodies and spaces under empire, this course invites students to rethink East Asia as a dynamic configuration of power, movement, and lived experience.
本課程以批判史學轉向、群島思維與身體政治為線索，探討現代東亞在帝國與戰爭條件下的歷史構成。課程超越國族中心敘事，檢視殖民現代性與空間想像如何形塑台灣、日本/沖繩、朝鮮半島、香港及太平洋區域的歷史經驗。第一單元「群島轉向」以文化轉向與殖民現代性辯論為起點，透過 Geoff Eley、Tani Barlow 與 Arif Dirlik 的討論，反思「區域」概念的形成與限制。在此基礎上本課程建立「群島轉向」的視角，將東亞理解為流動且相互連結的知識生產與權力空間，而非固定的地理框架。
第二單元「帝國下的身體」探討帝國權力如何透過飢餓、健康、生殖與種族化等機制運作。議題包括飢餓科學與地緣政治、優生學與總動員戰爭、台港殖民治理，以及沖繩「蘇鐵地獄」所反映的身體、種族及治理議題；探究身體如何成為帝國支配與動員的核心場域。
第三單元「空間化東亞」關注東亞政治的地景與秩序，分析戰爭時期至戰後亞洲的權力地景如何在洞窟、「營」與拘禁場所中重組。從沖繩戰的gama (ガマ)到台灣、東南亞的戰俘營，本單元探討空間如何成為壓迫、生存與歷史記憶共存的場所。透過「液態東亞」的視角，本課程最後將「東亞」延伸為一種群島式的空間政治線索，提供探索當代知識生產與權力形構的新視野。

crs_outline: 本課程將介紹具有深度社會反思精神的現代文學作品，我們將著重探討魯迅、沈從文、丁玲、卡夫卡等著名中外作家的代表作，相互參照比較，並參考相關重要的文學評論。本課程的教學將透過深入細緻解讀文學與歷史作品，配合相關的影像作品，藉以提升學生的文本解讀能力並訓練同學文學批評的方法，強化獨立思考與批判思辨的能力，養成扎實嚴謹的研究態度。期使學生能由點而面較為深入理解現代文學與歷史、虛構與社會現實之間的複雜關聯，同時藉由作家與歷史交錯結合，形塑具體歷史感受與倫理思維，以期達成認識現代社會與傳承文化經典的目標。

Students who are taking this course for the first time: Please email me, introduce yourself, and obtain my permission before taking the course.

Students interested in pursuing a research, art, film/media, or curatorial project in the above or related fields are very welcome to work with me. I will train students to hone their research skills, including analytical reading, analytical writing, theory analysis, film/art/media analysis, building up a bibliography /or filmography, etc., so that students can work on their M.A. theses, Ph.D. dissertations, film/art/media projects, or curatorial projects and complete them in a timely fashion.

Those interested in taking this course should contact me via email no later than the first week of the semester. Please introduce yourself to me and let me know your research interests. Our work will begin from there.

本課程目標為協助個別同學依據自己的興趣學習做研究，以完成自己的博士與碩士論文, 或電影、錄像、攝影、或其他媒體與藝術形式、或策展作品。課程設計請修課學生第一次修此課前，先寫信自我介紹，得到同意之後再選修。

dep_ename: Institute for Social Research and Cultural Studies
crs_outline:
本課程為文化研究之入門概論，以「人民／民眾／大眾」為核心主題，引領學生認識文化研究的主要理論取向與分析方法。「大眾」既是現代政治動員的對象、文化生產的受眾，也是媒介中介的主體，其概念本身即折射出文化研究跨學科、多向度的知識關懷。本課程藉由聚焦這一主題，帶領學生掌握文化研究的問題意識與核心論爭。
課程分三個單元展開。第一單元「諸民之辨」從政治哲學切入，辨析「人民」概念在現代語境中的多重形態——從無民到民粹，從民族自決到社會運動——揭示「民」作為政治主體的內在張力與歷史變遷。第二單元轉向文化史與文化社會學，透過Burke、Adorno、Bourdieu、Gramsci等人的經典文本，考察大眾文化如何在與精英文化的對立中被定義，如何成為霸權競逐的場域，以及如何在新自由主義治理下重塑主體性。第三單元「Mediating the Mass」則引入媒介理論，從海德格、班雅明、克拉考爾到霍爾、麥克魯漢、基特勒，探討媒介如何構成大眾感知與認同的基礎設施，並延伸至當代平台文化與粉絲經濟的討論。
三個單元雖各有理論重心，卻共享一個問題意識：面對「人民／民眾／大眾」這一充滿爭議的概念，文化研究如何以跨學科的視野，揭示其中複雜交織的權力關係、文化實踐與認同政治。修習本課程，學生將獲得進入文化研究領域的基本理論裝備與批判性閱讀能力。

crs_outline:
本課程以「經典、品味與權力」為題，從文化研究的視角探討文學與藝術如何被生產、命名、區分、消費與爭奪。課程關注的不只是作品本身，而是作品如何在特定的社會關係、制度安排與歷史脈絡中取得意義與價值。我們將討論：什麼能被稱為經典？誰有資格定義品味？文化價值如何與階級、性別、教育、市場、媒介與權力結構交織？課程將結合理論閱讀與具體案例，處理作者、觀眾、文化資本、經典形成、展示制度、文化工業，以及數位平台等議題，並思考文學與藝術如何不只是再現社會，也參與建構社會現實。透過跨越文學研究、藝術社會學、文化理論與文化政治的討論，本課程旨在引導學生理解文化價值從來不是自然存在，而是在不斷的分類、鬥爭與協商中被形塑。課程特別適合對文化研究、文學、藝術、社會理論與當代文化政治有興趣的研究生。
課程目標
修課完成後，學生應能：
理解文學與藝術研究中的主要社會理論問題與爭議。
辨識不同理論傳統對作品、作者、價值、制度與觀眾的不同理解。
以社會理論語彙分析具體的文學或藝術現象。
建立比較不同理論立場的能力，而非只停留在作者或概念羅列。

crs_outline:
隨著人工智慧（Artificial Intelligence, AI）的飛速發展，AI 已經成為提升各種應用體驗的重要工具。從聊天機器人到個人化推薦系統，AI能夠為使用者提供高度個人化體驗。本課程旨在探討AI 與使用者互動（AI-User Interaction） 的核心理論，並協助學生探索與應用 AI 技術於人機互動設計，同時著重於如何透過 AI 強化使用者的互動體驗。

課程目標：
1.	掌握人工智慧、機器學習、深度學習與自然語言處理等核心理論。
2.	建立 Python 程式設計與 AI 開發工具的基礎能力。
3.	利用AI 工具進行互動設計應用，轉化為創新的人機互動體驗。

網路社群的發展與型態日新月異，本課程著眼時下最流行的社群媒體（social media），介紹當前各種相關的研究議題。從傳播學、心理學、社會學等領域的研究成果中，賞析社群媒體的研究者如何探討使用者行為和效果，以及影響使用者互動的諸多因素，以更進一步了解晚近網路社群媒介對個人、社會的形塑。透過每週閱讀、課堂討論與反思，學生將能：

1. 掌握現今社群媒體的相關研究議題
2. 了解社群媒體研究的研究過程與方法
3. 評析傳播理論在社群媒體研究中的實用性
4. 發想並執行以社群媒體為主題的研究

cos_ename: Motion Capture and Future Interaction Technology Research
crs_outline:
課程概述與目標：
本綱要僅供選課參考，正式授課大綱將於開學第一週於課堂中公布。

Motion Capture (MoCap) plays a crucial role in various Virtual Reality and Metaverse applications. In this course, we discuss how MoCap technology tracks and records users movements, such as hand tracking, full-body tracking, eye tracking, and face tracking. The course is designed for beginners, explaining the basics of motion capture, including hardware and software. These concepts can be applied in future Virtual and Augmented Reality-mediated communication, such as user-driven avatars, bringing our creative visions of future human-computer interaction to life.

動作捕捉在各種虛擬實境和元宇宙應用扮演關鍵角色。在這門課，我們討論如何透過動作捕捉技術追蹤和紀錄使用者的各種動作，例如手部追蹤、全身追蹤、眼球和表情追蹤，本課程是為初學者設計，講解動作捕捉基礎知識，包括硬體和軟體內容。這些概念可以應用於未來虛擬和擴增實境中介傳播，例如使用者動作即時呈現的虛擬化身，將我們對未來人機互動的創意願景變為現實。

課程概述： ***本課程適合從未修習過心理與教育統計相關課程的學習者。***
＊本課程介紹理論與實務心理與行為研究中使用基本統計概念，包含敘述統計、中央極限定理、相關性與平均數比較的統計推論。
＊欲修課生請務必參加第一堂課程上午8點的統計檢定考試(考試結果不納入期末成績計算)。教育研究所碩博士生通過檢定考，獲免修本課資格後，請逕行另選進階統計方法課程進修。免修名單於統計檢定考試後一週內以email通知通過學生。
＊為培養跨域數據分析能力，本課程主要以R程式語言進行資料整理與統計分析。有任何問題請盡量與教學團隊討論。本課程相關作業皆以SPSS/R完成作業。
＊本課程作業請與同學/教學團隊公開討論，但必須親自完成。如經查證確認違反學術倫理，該項成績零分計算。期中考為紙本閉書考試，若抄襲舞弊將依校規議處。

課程目標：
1.	解基本統計概念、邏輯與實作分析技巧。
2.	具備解析與撰寫統計分析結果能力。
3.	了解量化研究設計概念與統計的關係。
4.	具備嚴謹數據思維、獨立思考的素養，與嫻熟初等統計分析的能力。

crs_outline:
課程概述：
本課程探討數位學習之基本概念，分為三個層次：（1）運用現況、（2）數位教材設計與教學策略、（3）理論與研究。本課程從探討資訊教育、數位學習的歷史與目標開始，進而探討數位學習在中小學、高等教育上的應用與策略，探討數位學習的設計、評量與研究趨勢。學生除了要修習相關的理論、並需設計教案、實際參與MOOCs課程之修課。

課程目標：
1. 瞭解資訊科技應用於教育的演變、理論與策略。
2. 瞭解數位學習在各學級上的應用。
3. 實際演練數位學習的教材設計與評量。
4. 熟習數位學習的論文架構與格式。
5. 分析數位學習的研究趨勢與議題。

cos_ename: Applied Multivariate Analysis and Machine Learning
crs_outline:
課程簡述：
本課程介紹教育領域常用之多變量分析及其實務應用，並進一步延伸至機器學習。目的為幫助學生透過多個分析方法的結果，從不同觀點探討教育現象背後的歷程。

課程目標：
(1) 能熟知研究問題所對應的多變量分析或機器學習方法
(2) 能適當應用統計軟體（例如Excel、JASP、R、Python）進行分析，並能正確解釋結果。
(3) 能根據各統計方法從不同觀點探討資料產生歷程，從而整合探討教育現象。

cos_cname: 進階科學課程與探究教學
crs_outline:
壹、本課程依據教師專業素養及其指標需求設計之教學內容如下:
本課程目標是讓修習學生瞭解科學探究的理論與評量，以及經由示範與討論如何應用在教學現場實務教學中，期望學生能夠學習到如何利用各種探究理論設計與評量探究課程，並且進一步做為研究或日後教學的基礎。

貳、本課程對應之師培中心教育目標、教師專業素養及其指標如下:
一、教育目標:
(一)培育具教育專業理念且熟悉教育實務的中學教師
(二)培養師資生具備以學生為本的教學素養
(三)發展師資生多元適性的教學知能
(四)培植師資生具創造正向學習環境的能力
(五)深化師資生的教師專業倫理與專業成長
二、教師專業素養及其指標:
(一)了解教育發展的理念與實務: 1-1 了解有關教育目的和價值的主要理論或思想，以建構自身的教育理念與信念。1-2 敏銳覺察社會環境對學生學習影響，以利教育機會均等。1-3 了解我國教育政策、法規及學校實務，以作為教育實踐的基礎。
(二)了解並尊重學習者的發展與學習需求: 2-1 了解並尊重學生身心發展、社經及文化背景的差異，以作為教學與輔導的依據。2-2 了解並運用學習原理，以符合學生個別的學習需求與發展。2-3 了解特殊需求學生的特質及鑑定歷程，以提供適切的教育與支持。
(三) 規劃適切的課程、教學及多元評量: 3-1 依據課程綱要/大綱、課程理論及教學原理，以規劃素養導向課程、教學及評量。3-2 依據課程綱要/大綱、課程理論及教學原理，以協同發展跨領域/群科/科目課程、教學及評量。3-3 具備任教領域/群科/科目所需的專門知識與學科教學知能，以進行教學。3-4 掌握社會變遷趨勢與議題，以融入課程與教學。3-5 應用多元教學策略、教學媒材及學習科技，以促進學生有效學習。3-6 根據多元評量結果調整課程與教學，以提升學生學習成效。
(四) 建立正向學習環境並適性輔導: 4-1 應用正向支持原理，共創安全、友善及對話的班級與學習環境，以養成學生良好品格及有效學習。4-2 應用輔導原理與技巧進行學生輔導，以促進適性發展。
(五) 認同並實踐教師專業倫理: 5-1 思辨與認同教師專業倫理，以維護學生福祉。5-2 透過教育實踐關懷弱勢學生，以體認教師專業角色。5-3 透過教育實踐與省思，以發展溝通、團隊合作、問題解決及持續專業成長的意願與能力。

This course explores the theory, research, and practice of mobile learning. In this course, you will be taught how to design, conduct, and evaluate the mobile learning environment. 
The course is designed for students to achieve the following goals:
Evaluate the potential of mobile learning in the e-learning era by critically analyzing current research on mobile learning affordances and challenges.
To evaluate the effectiveness of existing mobile learning solutions, including strategies, technologies, and learning materials.
To describe m-learning solutions includes strategies and technologies that can be applied in given contexts.
To develop appropriate mobile learning strategies that integrate existing learning and teaching theories.
Synthesize various instructional design frameworks and describe their application in a mobile learning instructional design context.
Discuss common issues related to the adaptation of mobile learning.

crs_outline: The aim of this course is to help student to understand the background knowledge of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and their applications in the brain science research through lectures. This course will also cover the fundamentals of the data analysis, including the data preprocessing, statistical analysis and group analysis. It also compares the model-based methods to the data-driven ones to fit the data analysis requirements in different experimental designs. Students are required to complete the assigned homework, read and present self-selected journal articles, and more importantly, design and conduct an fMRI experiment accordingly and analyze the fMRI data collected from the experiment. At the end of this course, the students should have hand-on experience in designing and conducting an fMRI experiment as well as analyzing the fMRI data from a single-subject session.

課程概述： ***本課程適合從未修習過心理與教育統計相關課程的學習者。***
＊本課程介紹理論與實務心理與行為研究中使用基本統計概念，包含敘述統計、中央極限定理、相關性與平均數比較的統計推論。

＊為培養跨域數據分析能力，本課程主要以R程式語言進行資料整理與統計分析。有任何問題請盡量與教學團隊討論。本課程相關作業皆以SPSS/R完成作業。
＊本課程作業請與同學/教學團隊公開討論，但必須親自完成。如經查證確認違反學術倫理，該項成績零分計算。期中考為紙本閉書考試，若抄襲舞弊將依校規議處。

1.	解基本統計概念、邏輯與實作分析技巧。

dep_ename: Institute of Foreign Literatures and Linguistics
crs_outline:
The characterization of human language under the generative framework since Chomsky (1957) consists of two major insights:
it is a "biological" entity, and it operates in a "computational/generative" manner (i.e., it is precise and formally explicit).

The focus of this course is the computational/generative aspect under this framework.
If you would like to know more about the biological aspect (which would give you a wider perspective of linguistics), please take my course "Language and the Human Mind."

The goal of this course is to provide an introduction to generative syntax (starting from 1957), from a cross-linguistic perspective. 
The course does not aim to make the students familiar with all the literature published within this theoretical framework, but rather to enable them to read this literature themselves, to understand it and to evaluate it independently.
I do not attempt to present the full intricacy of today’s version of “the best theory,” so I forsake some points of formalization and of how details are resolved, in favor of stressing important ideas and questions and how they have developed.
As a result, students will become acquainted with the history and general content of generative grammar and – most important in an ever-changing field – with how linguists actually develop their theories.
